title: Participation and Service
heading: ARTICLE III – Participation and Service
start_phrase: A Participant’ s entitlement to a Pension and to a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension for his Eligible Spouse shall be determined under Article IV based upon his period of Service.
summary:
- Excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program, following a clause on how paragraph and subparagraph references apply.
- Article III (Participation and Service):
  - Defines when an employee is a Participant: during periods when the employee would be currently entitled to a pension if employment ended, or would be entitled but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
  - States that entitlement to a Pension and a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is based on the Participant’s period of Service, with Service determined by Article III of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
  - Provides that the amount of both the Participant’s Pension and the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is based on Credited Service, also determined under Article III of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
- Article IV (Requirements for Benefits):
  - Establishes that Participants may receive a Pension and surviving Eligible Spouses may receive certain survivor benefits under this Article, with benefit amounts determined under Article V.
  - Specifies eligibility for a Normal Retirement Pension by reference to the requirements in Section 4.1 of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
text:
ARTICLE III – Participation and Service
3.1    Participation : An Employee shall be a Participant in the Plan during the period:
(a)    When he would be currently entitled to receive a Pension under the Plan if his employment
terminated at such time, or
(b)    When he would be so entitled but for the vesting requirement of Section 4.7.
3.2    Service . A Participant’ s entitlement to a Pension and to a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension for his
Eligible Spouse shall be determined under Article IV based upon his period of Service. A Participant’ s period of
Service shall be determined under Article III of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
3.3    Credited Service . The amount of a Participant’ s Pension and a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension shall
be based upon the Participant’ s period of Credited Service, as determined under Article III of Part C of the Salaried
Plan.

title: Requirements for Benefits - Introduction
heading: ARTICLE IV – Requirements for Benefits
start_phrase: A Participant shall be entitled to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse shall be entitled to certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article.
summary: Outlines eligibility for benefits under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program, specifying that pension and survivor benefit amounts are determined under Article V. It cross-references the Salaried Plan (Part C) for eligibility to Normal (Sec. 4.1), Early (Sec. 4.2), Late (Sec. 4.4), and Disability Pensions, with Late Retirement benefits beginning at the Late Retirement Date and disregarding ERISA §203(a)(3)(B) suspension notice and Part C Sec. 5.6(d) adjustments. A Vested Pension is available if vested under Sec. 4.7 and employment ends before Normal/Early Retirement; no benefit if vesting is not met. Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pensions begin when the corresponding Salaried Plan benefit begins and continue for the Eligible Spouse’s life, for survivors of active/disabled/retired and vested terminated employees, with amounts per Sec. 5.3 and subject to Sec. 4.9. When Pre-Retirement Spouse’s coverage is in effect, the participant’s pension under Sec. 5.2(b) is reduced annually by age-based charges: up to 35: 0%; 35–39: .075%; 40–44: .1%; 45–49: .175%; 50–54: .3%; 55–59: .5%; 60–64: .5%, pro rata for partial years and excluding the 90 days post-termination. Vesting follows the Salaried Plan, and Pre-409A pension payments commence per Sec. 6.1.

Requirements for Benefits
A Participant shall be entitled to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse shall be entitled to certain
survivor benefits as provided in this Article. The amount of any such Pension or survivor benefit shall be determined
in accordance with Article V .
4.1    Normal Retirement Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for a Normal Retirement Pension if he meets
the requirements for a Normal Retirement Pension in Section 4.1 of Part C of the Salaried Plan.

4.2    Early Retirement Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for an Early Retirement Pension if he meets the
requirements for an Early Retirement Pension in Section 4.2 of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
4.3    Vested Pension:  A Participant who is vested under Section 4.7 shall be eligible to receive a V ested
Pension if his employment in an eligible classification under the Salaried Plan is terminated before he is eligible for a
Normal Retirement Pension or an Early Retirement Pension. A Participant who terminates employment prior to
satisfying the vesting requirement in Section 4.7 shall not be eligible to receive a Pension under this Plan.

shall not receive a Pension until his Late Retirement Date. Thereafter , a Participant shall be eligible for a Late

any requirement for notice of suspension under ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) or any adjustment as under Section
5.6(d) of Part C of the Salaried Plan).
4.5    Disability Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for a Disability Pension if he meets the requirements for
a Disability Pension under the Salaried Plan.
4.6    Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension . Any Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension payable under this section
shall commence as of the same time as the corresponding pre-retirement spouse’ s pension under the Salaried Plan
and, subject to Section 4.9, shall continue monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse.

under this subsection to a Participant’ s Eligible Spouse (if any) who is entitled under the Salaried Plan to the special
pre-retirement spouse’ s pension for survivors of

title: Cashout Distributions
heading: 4.9 Cashout Distributions .
start_phrase: Notwithstanding the availability or applicability of a dif ferent form of payment under Article VI, the following rules shall apply in the case of certain small benefit Annuity payments:
summary:
- Cashout Distributions (Section 4.9): Establishes rules for mandatory lump-sum cashouts of small Pre-409A Pension benefits.
  - Participant pensions: If the Actuarial Equivalent lump-sum value at the Annuity Starting Date is at or below the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator must pay a lump sum; for Annuity Starting Dates before December 1, 2012, the threshold is $10,000.
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension: Same cashout rule and thresholds apply to Eligible Spouses; $10,000 threshold for Annuity Starting Dates before December 1, 2012.
  - Special discretionary cashouts of Vested Pensions: The Plan Administrator may cash out, in a single lump sum, Pre-409A Vested Pensions that have not begun, are at or below the Cashout Limit, and are practicable to calculate and distribute:
    - On December 1, 2012, with written list finalized by November 30, 2012.
    - On the first day of specified months in 2013 or 2014, with written list finalized by the day before the selected date.
  - Any lump sum is in lieu of the annuity otherwise payable. Provisions are intended to preserve grandfathered Pre-409A status and conform to Treasury Regulations on limited cashouts (Treas. Reg. §§ 1.409A-3(j)(4)(v), 1.409A-6(a)(4)(i)(E)). No participant or spouse may elect whether to be cashed out.

- Coordination with Long-Term Disability (Section 4.10): For periods prior to April 14, 1991, a participant cannot receive a Normal, Early, Vested, or Disability Pension for any month they are eligible for and receiving employer long-term disability benefits. An Eligible Spouse’s entitlement to a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or QJSA benefits is not negated by the participant’s receipt of long-term disability at death.

- Reemployment (Section 4.11): If a participant is reemployed and eligible to re-participate in the Salaried Plan after their Annuity Starting Date, payment of this plan’s pension is suspended if the Salaried Plan pension is (or would be) suspended. Payments recommence per Section 6.1, even if the Salaried Plan suspension ends earlier.

9    Cashout Distributions . Notwithstanding the availability or applicability of a dif ferent form of payment

title: Coordination with Long Term Disability Plan
heading: 4.10 Coordination with Long T erm Disability Plan .
start_phrase: The terms of this section apply notwithstanding the preceding provisions of this Article.
summary:
- Lump-sum cashouts under Section 4.9 are paid in lieu of the pension otherwise payable and are intended to preserve the grandfathered status of Pre-409A pensions by conforming to the “limited cashout” rules under Treasury Regulations §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v) and §1.409A-6(a)(4)(i)(E); no participant or eligible spouse may elect whether the vested or pre-retirement spouse’s pension is cashed out.
- Coordination with Long-Term Disability: For periods prior to April 14, 1991, a participant cannot receive a normal, early, vested, or disability pension for any month they are eligible for and receiving employer long-term disability benefits; however, an eligible spouse remains eligible for a pre-retirement spouse’s pension or Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity benefits if the participant dies while receiving LTD.
- Reemployment rules: If a participant is reemployed after their annuity starting date and becomes eligible to re-participate in the Salaried Plan, their Pension payments are suspended to the extent the Salaried Plan pension is (or would be) suspended; payments then recommence at the time specified under Section 6.1, even if the Salaried Plan suspension ends earlier.

title: Reemployment of Certain Participants
heading: 4.11 Reemployment of Certain Participants .
start_phrase: In the case of a current or former Participant who is reemployed and is eligible to reparticipate in the Salaried Plan after his Annuity Starting Date, payment of his Pension will be suspended if payment of his Salaried Plan pension is suspended (or would have been if it were already in pay status).
summary:
- Cashout rules (Section 4.9): Any lump-sum paid under this section replaces the pension otherwise payable to the participant or eligible spouse. The cashout features are intended to comply with Treasury Regulations on “limited cashouts” to preserve the grandfathered status of Pre‑409A pensions, and must be applied consistently with those rules. Participants and eligible spouses have no direct or indirect election over whether vested or pre‑retirement spouse’s pensions are cashed out.

- Coordination with Long-Term Disability (Section 4.10): Despite earlier provisions, for any period before April 14, 1991, a participant cannot receive a normal, early, vested, or disability pension for months when they are eligible for and receiving employer‑provided long‑term disability benefits. However, an eligible spouse remains eligible for a pre‑retirement spouse’s pension or QJSA benefits if the participant was on long‑term disability at death.

- Reemployment (Section 4.11): If a participant is reemployed after their annuity starting date and can reparticipate in the Salaried Plan, payment of their Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) benefit is suspended whenever the Salaried Plan pension is (or would be) suspended. Payments resume at the time specified under Section 6.1.

- Article V – Amount of Retirement Pension: The pension amount is determined under Sections 5.1–5.3, subject to adjustments in Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5.
  - Section 5.1 (PEP Pension):
    - Same form/time as Salaried Plan: PEP benefit equals Total Pension minus Salaried Plan Pension, both measured in the same form and commencement date.
    - Different form/time: PEP benefit equals the Total Pension in the PEP form/time multiplied by a fraction: (value of Total Pension minus value of Salaried Plan Pension) divided by value of Total Pension. Values are determined on a reasonable, consistent basis by the Plan Administrator for similarly situated employees.

title: PEP Pension
heading: 5.1 PEP Pension :
start_phrase: Same Form as Salaried Plan: If a Participant’ s Pension will be paid in the same form and will commence as of the same time as his pension under the Salaried Plan, then his Pension hereunder shall be the difference between:
summary:
- Article V sets out how a Participant’s retirement pension under the Plan is calculated, using Sections 5.1, 5.2, or 5.3, and subject to adjustments in Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5.
- Section 5.1 (PEP Pension) defines how the Plan benefit coordinates with the Salaried Plan:
  - Same form/time as Salaried Plan: the Plan benefit equals Total Pension minus the Salaried Plan Pension, both expressed in the same form and commencement date.
  - Different form/time: the Plan benefit equals the Total Pension in the Plan’s chosen form/time multiplied by a fraction: (value of Total Pension − value of Salaried Plan Pension) ÷ value of Total Pension. Values are determined on a reasonable and consistent basis by the Plan Administrator for similarly situated employees.
- Definitions for Section 5.1:
  - Total Pension is the greater of: (i) the Salaried Plan benefit calculated without the Code section 401(a)(17) and 415 limits and without the actuarial adjustment in Salaried Plan Part C §5.6(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2. Calculations match the specific form and timing; for lump sums, Actuarial Equivalent factors from Article II apply instead of those in the Salaried Plan.
  - Salaried Plan Pension means the benefit determined under the terms of the Salaried Plan.
- Section 5.2 (PEP Guarantee):
  - Applies only to Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings.
  - 1988 pensionable earnings are defined as remuneration for 1988 recognized for benefits under the then-effective Salaried Plan.
  - For ineligible Participants, the PEP Guarantee does not apply.

title: PEP Guarantee
heading: 5.2 PEP Guarantee :
start_phrase: A Participant who is eligible under subsection (a) below shall be entitled to a PEP Guarantee benefit determined under subsection (b) below .
summary:
- Defines “Total Pension” as the greater of: (i) the pension under the Salaried Plan calculated without IRC 401(a)(17) and 415 limits and without a specified actuarial adjustment, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2; calculated based on the elected form and timing of payment, with specified actuarial equivalent (AE) factors for lump sums.
- Defines “Salaried Plan Pension” as the pension amount under the Salaried Plan.
- Establishes PEP Guarantee eligibility for Participants with at least $75,000 of 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer, using earnings recognized under the 1988 Salaried Plan and excluding periods with non-Employers.
- Details PEP Guarantee benefit formulas:
  - Default Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service (CS) plus 1% of HAME for CS over 10 years, minus 1-2/3% of Primary Social Security Amount (PSSA) times CS up to 30 years. For Vested Pensions, the benefit is projected to Normal Retirement Age (NRA) for CS, with HAME and PSSA at severance, then prorated by actual CS over projected CS.
  - For employees in eligible Salaried Plan classifications before July 1, 1975: greater of Formula A or Formula B, with a note that Formula B’s subparagraph (ii)(B) does not apply to Vested Pensions.
  - Formula B: greater of (A) 1.5% of HAME × CS − 50% of PSSA, or (B) 3% of HAME × CS up to 15 years − 50% of PSSA.
  - Disability Pension under either formula uses CS per Salaried Plan rules and HAME/PSSA at disability date.
- Special calculation rules for PEP Guarantee:
  - Surviving Eligible Spouse’s annuity: 50% of the Participant’s annuity, with no reduction to the Participant; reduced if spouse is more than 10 years younger (−0.8% per full year ages 11–20 younger; additional −0.4% per year beyond 20).
  - Reductions:
    - Early retirement: 3/12 of 1% per month before NRA.
    - Vested Pension: AE reduction if commencement before NRA; apply Salaried Plan pre-retirement spouse coverage reductions.
    - If elected form provides a larger spouse survivor benefit than the standard 50%, or a non-spouse survivor, or includes inflation protection, reduce to AE of the standard benefit (single life or non-inflation-protected, as applicable).
  - Lump sum conversion: lump sum equals the AE of the PEP Guarantee including survivor benefit value and any early retirement reductions.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (Section 5.3): payable amount equals the difference between the Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension and the Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension; includes a definition of “Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension” (text continues beyond excerpt).

title: Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension
heading: 5.3 Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension :
start_phrase: The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Spouse under Section 4.6 shall be determined under subsection (a) below .
summary:
- Explains actuarial adjustments when optional annuity protections are elected, ensuring the total benefit value equals the actuarial equivalent of the elected annuity without such protection.
- Defines Lump Sum Conversion: a lump-sum distribution equals the actuarial equivalent of the participant’s PEP Guarantee, reflecting any survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.
- Sets the formula for the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (PRSP): the monthly benefit to a surviving Eligible Spouse equals the Eligible Spouse’s Total PRSP minus the Salaried Plan PRSP.
- Clarifies “Total PRSP” as the greater of: (i) the Salaried Plan PRSP calculated without Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and without a specific actuarial adjustment, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee PRSP; both measured at the applicable payment time.
- Details the PEP Guarantee PRSP:
  - Normal Rule: based on the survivor portion of a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity assuming separation at death (or severance date), commencement when spouse payments begin, and death immediately thereafter; includes early commencement reductions if before Normal Retirement Date.
  - Special Rule for active/disabled employees: minimum PRSP of 25% of the participant’s PEP Guarantee; Credited Service and pay/Social Security figures determined as specified; no early commencement reduction.
- Provides “Certain Adjustments”:
  - Defines “specified plan” (the Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified plans not based on pay deferrals, including the PepsiCo Prior Plan).
  - Requires recalculation for rehired participants whose Salaried Plan benefits are recomputed after their annuity start date; the Pre-409A Pension and PEP Guarantee are adjusted correspondingly for in‑service and prior distributions.

title: Certain Adjustments
heading: 5.4 Certain Adjustments :
start_phrase: Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to adjustment as provided in this section.
summary:
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension rules:
  - Standard early-commencement reductions apply to the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity base.
  - Special rule for active or disabled employees: minimum spouse’s benefit equals 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2), with Credited Service determined per Salaried Plan rules; earnings/social security metrics fixed at date of death; no early-commencement reduction under this special rule.

- Pension adjustments (Section 5.4):
  - Defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or certain nonqualified plans sponsored by a PBG Organization member and not based on pay deferrals (includes the PepsiCo Prior Plan).
  - Rehired participants: if the Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated after reemployment (post–Annuity Starting Date) for added Credited Service, the Pre-409A Pension and PEP Guarantee are also recalculated, adjusting for in-service and prior distributions and coordinating with benefits from this and any specified plans.
  - Increases under other plans: if a specified plan benefit rises after PEP benefits are set, PEP is recalculated; overpayments are recoverable; no duplication of payments across plans.

- Excludable employment (Section 5.5):
  - For employment on/after June 30, 1997, executives at level 22+ on limited-duration assignments do not earn a benefit or benefit increase tied to that assignment.

- Distribution options (Article VI; Section 6.1):
  - Governs form and timing of Pre-409A Pension distributions beginning on/after March 1, 1992; earlier distributions follow the Prior Plan.
  - All distributions subject to cashout rules in Section 4.9.
  - Introduces “No Advance Election” provisions for participants without an advance election in effect (text truncated).

4    Certain Adjustments : Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to
adjustment as provided in this section. For purposes of this section, “specified plan” shall mean the Salaried Plan or a
nonqualified pension plan similar to this Plan. A nonqualified pension plan is similar to this Plan if it is sponsored by a
member of the PBG Organization and if its benefits are not based on participant pay deferrals (this category of similar
plans includes the PepsiCo Prior Plan).
(a)    Adjustments for Rehired Participants : This subsection shall apply to a current or former Participant
who is reemployed after his Annuity Starting Date and whose benefit under the Salaried Plan is recalculated based
on an additional period of Credited Service. In the event of any such recalculation, the Participant’ s Pre-409A
Pension shall also be recalculated hereunder . For this purpose, the PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2 is adjusted for
in-service distributions and prior distributions in the same manner as benefits are adjusted
- 119 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Programunder the Salaried Plan, but by taking into account benefits under this Plan and any specified plans.
(b)    Adjustment for Increased Pension Under Other Plans : If the benefit paid under a specified plan on
behalf of a Participant is increased after PEP benefits on his behalf have been determined (whether the increase is
by order of a court, by agreement of the plan administrator of the specified plan, or otherwise), the PEP benefit for the
Participant shall be recalculated. If the recalculation identifies an overpayment hereunder , the Plan Administrator shall
take such steps as it deems advisable to recover the overpayment. It is specifically intended that there shall be no
duplication of payments under this Plan and any specified plans.

title: Excludable Employment
heading: 5.5 Excludable Employment :
start_phrase: Effective for periods of employment on or after June 30, 1997, an executive classified as level 22 or above whose employment by an Employer is for a limited duration assignment shall not become entitled to a benefit or to any increase in benefits in connection with such employment.
summary:
- Coordination with other plans: Benefits are determined by considering this Plan and specified plans together to avoid duplication. If a participant’s benefit under a specified plan is increased after PEP benefits are set, the PEP benefit is recalculated and any overpayment may be recovered.
- Excludable Employment: Effective June 30, 1997, executives at level 22 or above on limited-duration assignments do not accrue benefits or increases from that employment.
- Distribution Options (Article VI): Establishes how benefits are distributed when a participant becomes entitled to a pension.
- Form and Timing of Distributions (Section 6.1): Governs distributions of Pre‑409A pensions beginning on or after March 1, 1992; earlier distributions follow the prior plan; all distributions are subject to cashout rules in Section 4.9.
- No Advance Election (Section 6.1(a)): Provides rules for participants without an Advance Election in effect (details truncated).

title: Form and Timing of Distributions
heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions :
start_phrase: This section shall govern the form and timing of distributions of Pre-409A Pensions that begin on or after March 1, 1992.
summary:
- Coordination with other plans and overpayment recovery: If a participant’s benefit under a specified plan increases after PEP benefits are determined, the PEP benefit is recalculated to prevent duplication of payments, and any overpayment under the PEP may be recovered.  
- Excludable employment rule: Effective June 30, 1997, executives at level 22+ on limited-duration assignments do not earn PEP benefits or increases tied to that assignment.  
- Article VI scope: Governs how Pre-409A Pensions are distributed, applying to distributions starting on or after March 1, 1992, and subject to the Plan’s cashout rules.  
- Default distribution without an Advance Election: If no Advance Election is in place by the day before Retirement Date (or if employment ends before Retirement), the PEP benefit is paid in the same form and at the same time as the Salaried Plan benefit.  
- Special timing if still employed at Salaried Plan annuity start: If the Salaried Plan Annuity Starting Date occurs while the participant is still employed (due to Code section 401(a)(9)), PEP payments begin the first of the month after the Severance from Service Date, using the same form as the Salaried Plan.  
- Use of an Advance Election (for retirements after 1993): Must meet timing and procedural requirements; governs form and start date of PEP distributions.  
- Lump sum with Advance Election: If a Single Lump Sum is elected in advance, it is paid on the first of the month coincident with or following the Retirement Date.  
- Annuity with Advance Election: If an annuity is elected in advance, it begins on the first of the month coincident with or following the Retirement Date.  
- Determining annuity form when an annuity is elected:  
  - If there is a qualifying Salaried Plan election specifying an annuity (in effect as of the day before Retirement Date), the PEP annuity mirrors that form.  
  - If no qualifying Salaried Plan election, but a PEP Election exists, the PEP pays the annuity form chosen in the PEP Election.  
  - If neither election applies, default is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married, or a Single Life Annuity if unmarried (marital status measured the day before Retirement Date).  
- Available forms reference: Section 6.2 notes that specified forms of payment are available to any participant entitled to a Retirement Pension (details follow beyond the excerpt).

title: Available Forms of Payment
heading: 6.2 Available Forms of Payment :
start_phrase: The forms of payment set forth in subsections (a) and (b) may be provided to any Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension.
summary:
- Establishes the hierarchy for determining a participant’s payout form:
  - If there is a qualifying Salaried Plan election in effect as of the day before Retirement Date and it specifies any annuity form (including when paired with a lump sum), the same annuity form applies.
  - If not, but a PEP Election is in effect as of the day before Retirement Date, the annuity form in that election applies.
  - If neither applies, the default is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity (QJSA) for married participants or a Single Life Annuity for unmarried participants; marital status is measured the day before Retirement Date.
- Lists available payment forms for Retirement Pensions (effective for Annuity Starting Dates after 1989; earlier distributions follow the Prior Plan):
  - Single Life Annuity (lifetime monthly payments ending at death).
  - Survivor annuities:
    - 100% Survivor Option (same reduced amount to beneficiary for life).
    - 75% Survivor Option (75% of reduced amount to beneficiary for life).
    - 50% Survivor Option (50% of reduced amount to beneficiary for life; counts as a QJSA if beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse).
    - Ten Years Certain and Life (lifetime payments with at least 120 monthly payments guaranteed to beneficiary if death occurs earlier).
  - Single Lump Sum payment.
  - Combination Lump Sum/Monthly Benefit (permitted only if no Advance Election is in effect), with participant-designated whole-number percentages that total 100%; lump sum and monthly portions are each prorated by the elected percentages.
- Describes optional inflation protection (not available on lump sums):
  - Two levels: 5% or 7% thresholds. Monthly benefits are initially reduced, then increased each January 1 (starting the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date) by the amount prior-year inflation exceeds the elected threshold.
  - Inflation measured over the 12 months ending September 30, using the method applicable to Social Security COLAs as of January 1, 1989.
  - Increases carry over to survivor benefits; elections are irrevocable by the participant and any surviving beneficiary.
- Specifies forms for vested (non-retirement) benefits:
  - Married participants: QJSA.
  - All participants: Single Life Annuity is available.
  - Specific form determined under Section 6.1(a).
- Outlines election procedures (Advance Elections and PEP Elections):
  - Must be made in writing on a Plan Administrator–designated form and signed by the participant (section continues beyond the excerpt).

(i)    100 percent Survivor Option : The Participant shall receive a reduced Pension payable

for life, ending with the last monthly payment due prior to his death. Payments in the amount of 50
percent of such reduced Pension shall be continued after the Participant’ s death to his beneficiary for
life, beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’ s death and
ending with the last monthly payment due prior to the beneficiary’ s death. A 50 percent survivor option
under this paragraph shall be a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant’ s beneficiary is his

(iv)    Ten Years Certain and Life Option : The Participant shall receive a reduced Pension
which shall be payable monthly for his lifetime but for not less than 120 months. If the retired Participant
dies before 120 payments have been made, the monthly Pension amount shall be paid for the
remainder of the 120 month period to the Participant’ s primary beneficiary (or if the primary beneficiary

title: Procedures for Elections
heading: 6.3 Procedures for Elections :
start_phrase: This section sets forth the procedures for making Advance Elections and PEP Elections.
summary:
- 7% inflation protection option: Monthly benefits are initially reduced but increase each January 1 if prior-year inflation exceeds 7%, by the amount over 7%. First increase occurs the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date. Inflation is measured over the 12 months ending September 30 using the Social Security COLA method in effect on January 1, 1989. Protection carries over to survivor benefits, and the election is irrevocable.
- Vested benefit forms: Married Participants receive a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity; a Single Life Annuity is available to both married and unmarried Participants, per Section 6.1(a).
- Election procedures (Section 6.3): Elections and revocations must be written, on Plan forms, and signed; no spousal consent required.
- Advance Election: 
  - Made on/after July 15, 1993; choose Annuity or Single Lump Sum.
  - Must be received before the start of the calendar year containing the Retirement Date and at least 6 months before the Retirement Date.
  - Remains effective until changed by a new timely election; revocable only if revocation meets the same timing; void if no entitlement to a Retirement Pension.
- PEP Election:
  - Available only if an Advance Election for an Annuity is in effect (advance receipt rule is deemed met if it will be by the proposed Retirement Date).
  - Participant selects an annuity form from Section 6.2 and may elect inflation protection; forms in 6.2(a)(3) and (4) are not available via PEP.
  - Must be received 90 days to the day before the Retirement Date; beneficiary age proof due by the day before the Retirement Date if required for reductions.
  - Can be changed by a new timely PEP Election; becomes effective at close of business the day before Retirement Date; void if no Advance Election in effect.
- Annuity Starting Date rules: Elections at an Annuity Starting Date apply to all unpaid accruals then due. If rehired after an initial Annuity Starting Date (with an annuity in pay or after a prior lump sum other than a small cashout), subsequent elections apply only to benefits accruing after rehire; prior accruals continue under prior elections.
- Receipt timing: An election is treated as received if postmarked that day or actually received by the Plan Administrator by close of business (as determined by the Administrator).
- Survivor options—effect of death around PEP Elections: If the Participant or beneficiary dies before a PEP Election (for forms under 6.2(a)(2)) becomes effective, the election is disregarded. If the Participant dies after the PEP Election is effective but before payments begin, the election is honored; survivor benefits start the first day of the month after death, with any back payments to the Participant’s estate.

start_phrase: If a Participant makes a PEP Election for a form of payment described in Section 6.2(a)(2) and the Participant or his beneficiary (beneficiaries in the case of Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)) dies before the PEP Election becomes ef fective, the election shall be disregarded.
summary:
- Rehired participants after an initial Annuity Starting Date:
  - If already receiving an annuity in pay status upon rehire, or previously took a lump sum (other than a Section 4.9(a) cashout), any new Annuity Starting Date and related elections apply only to benefits accrued after rehire.
  - Prior accruals continue to be paid under the elections made at the initial Annuity Starting Date.
- Election timing:
  - An election is treated as received if postmarked that day or actually received by the Plan Administrator by close of business (as determined by the Administrator).
- Special rules for survivor options (Section 6.4):
  - Effect of certain deaths:
    - If the Participant or beneficiary dies before a PEP Election becomes effective, the election is disregarded.
    - If the Participant dies after the PEP Election becomes effective but before payments start, the elected form is honored; survivor benefits begin the first day of the month after death, and any back payments due to the Participant are paid to the estate.
    - For the option in Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv): if the Participant dies after the PEP Election is effective, has no surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and before receiving 120 payments, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate. If a beneficiary had begun receiving payments and dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
  - Nonspouse beneficiary age limits:

    - 75% survivor option is not permitted if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 19 years younger than the Participant.
- Beneficiary designations (Section 6.5):
  - Required for forms with survivor options; made on a PEP Election Form or applicable Salaried Plan form.
  - For the Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv) option, both a primary and contingent beneficiary may be named.
  - Participants may change or revoke beneficiary designations any time before the election is finally effective, subject to Plan Administrator rules.
  - A designation (or change/revocation) is not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.

title: 1993 Accruals
heading: ARTICLE A – 1993 Accruals
start_phrase: This Article A of the Appendix shall be ef fective on the date the Plan is adopted.
summary:
- Article A – 1993 Accruals: Effective upon plan adoption; establishes who qualifies for special 1993 accrual treatment and how benefits are calculated.
  - Eligibility: Salaried Plan Participants employed on December 31, 1993, vested in 1993 (or would vest in 1994 with assumed continued service), and whose minimum 1993 Pension is not derived solely from the portion described in Article X(c) of the main plan.
  - Minimum 1993 Pension: Accrued as of December 31, 1993, using assumptions that:
    - Service and Credited Service continue through December 31, 1994, unless HR records show a scheduled 1994 termination, in which case only through that date.
    - Highest Average Monthly Earnings are projected to end of 1994 using the plan’s actuarial salary scale; a higher “Special PEP Salary Scale” is used if it projects higher 1994 earnings; if service is assumed to end during 1994, earnings after termination are excluded.
    - Attained age is assumed as of the end of the assumed continued service period.
  - Vesting: Any covered individual not otherwise vested becomes vested as of December 31, 1993 in both the regular Pension and the minimum 1993 Pension.
  - Limits: Code section 401(a)(17) applies for 1993 as amended by OBRA 1993.
  - Later Accruals: For participants with a minimum 1993 Pension, any Pre‑409A Pension accrued after 1993 is only the amount exceeding that minimum.

- Article P98 – PepsiCo Special Early Retirement Benefit: Supplements the main plan for certain employees effective February 1, 1998.

title: PepsiCo Special Early Retirement Benefit
heading: ARTICLE P98 – PepsiCo Special Early Retirement Benefit
start_phrase: This Article supplements the main portion of the Plan document with respect to the rights and benefits of Covered Employees on and after the Ef fective Date.
summary:
- Article P98 establishes a Special Early Retirement Benefit under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre‑409A Program for certain “Covered Employees” effective February 1, 1998.
- Covered Employee is defined as an employee ineligible for the Salaried Plan Early Retirement Benefit solely due to highly compensated status under the Legacy PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan provisions; other key definitions include Effective Date, Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit, and Severance Date (an eligible involuntary termination).
- Benefit amount and form: A Covered Employee receives a single lump-sum payment, as soon as administratively practicable after the Severance Date, in lieu of any other benefits under the Plan. The lump sum equals:
  - The actuarial present value of the Total Pension as of the Severance Date, assuming eligibility for the Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit and commencement on the Severance Date,
  - Minus the actuarial present value of the Salaried Plan Pension as of the Severance Date, determined without this Appendix and assuming commencement at Normal Retirement Date.
- Calculations use actuarial equivalence factors in effect on the Severance Date for lump-sum conversions, assume a Single Life Annuity form, and, if applicable, substitute more favorable PEP Guarantee early commencement reduction factors (Section 5.2) for the Salaried Plan’s early reduction factors in determining the Total Pension component.
- Article IPO covers Transferred and Transition Individuals following the spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan, relying on definitions and terms in the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc.
- Rights preserved: Transferred Individuals participating in the PepsiCo Prior Plan immediately before the Effective Date become Participants in this Plan as of the Effective Date; the spin-off causes no break in Service or Credited Service for Transferred or Transition Individuals; service, compensation, and other benefit-affecting determinations are preserved per the Agreement as of the Close of the Distribution Date.

ARTICLE P AC
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
start_phrase: This Article P AC supplements the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan document with respect to the appointment of the members of the P AC.
summary:
- Establishes guiding principles for appointing members to PepsiCo’s Pension Administrative Committee (PAC) under the Pension Equalization Plan.
- Eligibility criteria: must be a PepsiCo employee at Band 1 or above, able to devote sufficient time, and possess the character and temperament to act prudently and solely in the interests of plan participants and beneficiaries.
- Additional membership guidelines: prior benefit plan administration or transferable ERISA-related experience; the committee collectively should have expertise across ERISA health, welfare, and retirement plans; each member must be able to evaluate the reasonableness of plan expenses.
- The PAC Chair may consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify qualified candidates.
- These guidelines are advisory to the Chair and do not alter ERISA’s legal standards.
- The excerpt also indicates a transition to the Section 409A Program Plan Document (January 1, 2022 Restatement).

ARTICLE P AC
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments     
PAC.1 Scope.  This Article P AC supplements the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan document with respect to
the appointment of the members of the P AC.
PAC.2 General Guidelines . To be a member of the P AC, an individual must:
(a)    Be an employee of the PepsiCo Organization at a Band 1 or above level,
(b)    Be able to give adequate time to committee duties, and
(c)    Have the character and temperament to act prudently and diligently in the exclusive interest of the
Plan’ s participants and beneficiaries.
PAC.3 PAC Guidelines . In addition to satisfying the requirements set forth in Section P AC.2, the following
guidelines will also apply to the P AC membership:
(a)    Each member of the P AC should have experience with benefit plan administration or other
experience that can readily translate to a role concerning ERISA plan administration,
(b)    The membership of the P AC as a whole should have experience and expertise with respect to the
administration of ERISA health and welfare and retirement plans, and
(c)    Each member of the P AC should be capable of prudently evaluating the reasonableness of
expenses that are charged to the Plan.
PAC.4 Additional Information . The Chair of the P AC may seek information from Company personnel, including
the Controller , CFO and CHRO, in connection with his identification of well qualified candidates for committee
membership.

title: Foreword
heading:
ARTICLE I
Foreword
start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
summary:
- Purpose and scope: The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) provides supplemental pension benefits to salaried employees who participate in the Salaried Plan, making up for benefits limited by Internal Revenue Code caps, and also includes certain benefits based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula for eligible employees.

- Restatement history: The Plan was restated in 1989, then comprehensively restated effective January 1, 2005 to establish the Section 409A program terms. Subsequent restatements occurred effective January 1 of 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2022 (the current restatement).

- Section 409A coverage: The 2005 restatement governs benefits subject to Section 409A (generally amounts earned or vested after December 31, 2004 or materially modified under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-6(a)(4)).

- Merger with PBG PEP: Effective December 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan merged into this Plan. The 409A PBG PEP document (as of April 1, 2009, amended through January 1, 2011) is attached as an appendix and continues to govern pre-merger PBG PEP 409A benefits, with certain administrative provisions now governed by the main 409A PepsiCo PEP document. The merger and updates did not change the time or form of payment for 409A benefits.

- Interplay of 409A and pre-409A programs: Benefits not subject to the 409A Program (generally earned or vested before January 1, 2005 and not materially modified) are governed by the Pre-409A Program document. Both documents together describe a single plan, but 409A and pre-409A amounts are tracked separately to preserve grandfathered, 409A-exempt status.

- Linkage to the Salaried Plan and 2025 freeze: PEP accruals and eligibility to “grow into” benefit enhancements generally mirror those under the Salaried Plan. Special provisions (including the “PEP Guarantee” in Section 5.2 and certain appendix provisions) may provide accruals beyond strict make-up for Code limits for some participants. The freeze of the Salaried Plan effective end of day December 31, 2025 also freezes all PEP accruals as of that time, and post-freeze grow-in rules follow the Salaried Plan’s operational rules.

- Definitions section begins: Article II introduces defined terms used throughout the document.

- Key defined terms excerpted:
  - Accrued Benefit: The pension payable at Normal Retirement Date per Article V, based on Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Credited Service at the determination date.
  - Actuarial Equivalent: A benefit of equal value determined using specified actuarial factors applied uniformly; new rights/features/benefits use these factors only if expressly adopted. For annuity forms (e.g., qualified joint and survivor, survivor annuities, inflation-protected annuities, period certain and life), the Plan Administrator selects the factors; effective January 1, 2009, factors are in Schedule 1 (prior factors in the appendix).

ARTICLE I
Foreword
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan. PEP provides
benefits for eligible employees whose pension benefits under the Salaried Plan are limited by the provisions of the
Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. In addition, PEP provides benefits for certain eligible employees based
on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula (see, for example, Part B thereof).
1989 Restatement . The Plan was amended and restated in its entirety in 1989.
409A Program Document 2005 Restatement . The Plan was last amended and restated in its entirety
effective as of January 1, 2005. The 2005 restatement sets forth the terms of the Plan that are applicable to benefits
that are subject to Section 409A, i.e., generally , benefits that are earned or vested after December 31, 2004 or
materially modified within the meaning of T reas. Reg. § 1.409A-6(a)(4) (the “409A Program”).
Amendments to the 2005 Restatement . The 2005 restatement was amended to reflect the merger into
this Plan of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PBG PEP”), ef fective at the end of the day on December 31, 2011.
The PBG PEP document that was in ef fect on April 1, 2009, as amended through January 1, 2011 (the “409A PBG

that were subject to the 409A PBG PEP Document prior to the Plan merger , except for certain administrative
provisions that are now governed by the main portion of the 409A PepsiCo PEP Document as is explained in

Internal Revenue Code Section 409A (“Section 409A”)

Interplay of this 409A Program and Pre-409A Program . All benefits under the Plan that are not subject

Program describe the terms of a single plan. However , amounts subject to the terms of this 409A Program and
amounts subject to the terms of the Pre-409A Program shall be tracked separately at all times. The preservation of
the terms of the Pre-409A Program, without material modification, and the separation between the 409A Program
amounts and the Pre-409A Program amounts are intended to be suf ficient to permit the pre-409A Program to remain
exempt from Section 409A as grandfathered benefits.
Freeze of the Salaried Plan . In general, the Plan provides benefits that make up for benefits that would
accrue under the Salaried Plan but for certain Code limitations on benefits and compensation that apply to the
Salaried Plan. As a result, a Participant’ s accrual of Plan benefits and a Participant’ s growing into certain benefit
enhancements (such as more favorable early commencement factors) are generally tied to the Participant’ s accrual
of benefits and growing into benefit enhancements under the Salaried Plan. For certain
- 2 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramParticipants, there are special provisions in Section 5.2 (the “PEP Guarantee”) or the Appendix that provide a benefit
accrual opportunity that goes beyond providing a make up for the application of Code limitations to the Salaried Plan.
Regardless, however , the freeze on accruals under the Salaried Plan that is ef fective as of the end of the day on
December 31, 2025 also freezes all accruals under this Plan ef fective as of that time. In addition, the Salaried Plan’ s
operational rules with respect to the ability to grow into benefit enhancements after December 31, 2025 govern the
ability to grow into benefit enhancements after December 31, 2025 under this Plan.
- 3 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program

summary:
- Scope: Article II (Definitions and Construction) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program and the start of Article III (Participation and Service).
- Actuarial Equivalent and payment factors: sets Plan Administrator authority over actuarial factors; includes Schedule 1 mortality tables and interest rates (GAR 94 through 12/31/2018; 2019 mortality table thereafter; distinct factors for 5% and 7% inflation protection); allows retroactive application with a floor tied to 2019 Salaried Plan factors; lump sums use Salaried Plan lump-sum factors; other adjustments follow Salaried Plan (including 2019 updates).
- Core plan definitions: Accrued Benefit, Annuity, Annuity Starting Date, Cashout Limit, Code, Company, Covered Compensation, Credited Service, Disability/Normal/Early/Late/ Vested 409A Pensions, Elapsed Time Service, Employee/Employer, ERISA, FICA Amount, 409A Program, Highest Average Monthly Earnings (without 401(a)(17) cap), Participant, Pension (409A vs. Pre-409A), Plan/Plan Year/Pre-409A Program, Salaried Plan, Section 409A, Service, Social Security Act, Taxable Wage Base.
- Spouse and partner eligibility: detailed post-1/1/2019 definition of Eligible Domestic Partner (civil union, health plan enrollment, or other written criteria; one partner maximum; cannot have both spouse and partner); Eligible Spouse defined under federal tax law.
- Governance: PepsiCo Administration Committee (PAC) composition, chair designation, appointment principles, expertise requirements, and semiannual activity reports; reference to Guiding Principles for appointments.
- Key Employee rules: identification under Code §§416/409A with officer/owner thresholds; administrative convenience adding Leadership Group 6+ (capped at 200); historical transition rules (2010–2018) across PepsiCo/PBG/PAS; timing of annual identification and effectiveness periods; compensation definition per Treas. Reg. §1.415(c)-2.
- Social Security coordination: Primary Social Security Amount assumptions for retirement/survivor and disability calculations (age-65 estimate rules, exclusions, law as of separation).
- Conduct restrictions: Prohibited Misconduct (competition in Covered Products, non-solicit, confidentiality breaches, code/securities violations, fraud) with DTSA and government reporting protections; broad “Participation” and detailed “Covered Products” definitions.
- Benefit forms and options: Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, Single Life Annuity, Single Lump Sum; survivor/period-certain and inflation-protection adjustments per schedules; pre-retirement spouse’s and domestic partner’s pensions.
- Separation from Service: 409A-compliant standards (20% service threshold; leave-of-absence rules including 6-month and 29-month disability substitutions; director services disregarded; certain transfers to 20%+ owned entities not separations); Final Separation from Service concept.
- Construction rules: grammar/number conventions; “hereof/hereunder” usage; “including” read as without limitation; document hierarchy and cross-reference conventions.
- Participation and Service (Article III start): who qualifies as a Participant (currently entitled or but for vesting; status may later cease); eligibility exclusions mirror the Salaried Plan; entitlement and pre-retirement survivor benefits based on Service determined under the Salaried Plan (noting an exception for certain inpats).

ARTICLE II
Definitions and Construction
2.1    Definitions : This section provides definitions for certain words and phrases listed below . Where the
following words and phrases, in boldface and underlined, appear in this Plan document (including the Foreword) with
initial capitals they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the
context.
Accrued Benefit : The Pension payable at Normal Retirement Date determined in accordance
with Article V , based on the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings and Credited Service at the date
of determination.
Actuarial Equivalent : Except as otherwise specifically set forth in the Plan or any Appendix to
the Plan with respect to a specific benefit determination, a benefit of equivalent value computed on the basis of
the factors set forth below . The application of the following assumptions to the computation of benefits payable
under the Plan shall be done in a uniform and consistent manner . In the event the Plan is amended to provide
new rights, features or benefits, the following actuarial factors shall not apply to these new elements unless
specifically adopted by the amendment.
(1)    Annuities and Inflation Protection : To determine the amount of a Pension payable in
the form of a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity or optional form of survivor annuity , as an annuity
with inflation protection, or as a period certain and life annuity , the Plan Administrator shall select the
factors that are to be used. Effective January 1, 2009, the factors selected by the Plan Administrator
are set forth in Schedule 1, below (prior factors appear in the Appendix). Thereafter , the Plan
Administrator shall review
- 4 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programsuch factors for forms of payment (including for annuities and lump sums) from time to time and shall
amend such factors in its discretion. In general, a Participant shall have no right to have any of the
actuarial factors specified for forms of payment under the Plan from time to time applied to his benefit
(or any portion thereof), except to the extent that a particular factor is currently in ef fect at the time it is
to be applied under the Plan. For the avoidance of doubt, it is expressly intended and binding upon
Participants that any actuarial factors for forms of payment selected by the Plan Administrator from
time-to-time may be applied retroactively to already accrued benefits, and without regard to the
actuarial factors that may have applied previously for such purpose. However , in adjusting benefits
under the Plan using those factors in Schedule 1 (below) that become ef fective for Annuity Starting
Dates on or after January 1, 2019, the right to receive a benefit that is not less than would have applied
under the prior basis for this adjustment shall apply to the same extent (and in the same manner) as
applies under the Salaried Plan with respect to the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors. For this purpose, the
phrase “2019 Salaried Plan Factors” refers to the new factors that appear in the Salaried Plan’ s
definition of “Actuarial Equivalent” ef fective for annuity starting dates (as defined under the Salaried
Plan) on or after January 1, 2019. Effective for Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019, if a
Participant elects a survivor , period certain annuity or other death benefit annuity with inflation
protection, Schedule 1(b) shall apply to adjust the Single Life Annuity for the survivor benefit, period
certain or other death benefit, and Schedule 1(c) or (d) shall apply solely to adjust for the
- 5 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programelected inflation protection (for this purpose and as applies generally when determining an Actuarial
Equivalent, the adjustment resulting from applying these factors from separate Schedules shall be
determined using an actuarial computation method that is reasonable and applied consistently to
similarly situated participants).

(2)    Lump Sums : To determine the lump sum value of a Pension, a Pre-Retirement
Spouse’ s Pension under Section 4.6, or a Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension under Section

under this Plan) on or after January 1, 2019. These factors are subject to change in accordance with

Annuity : A Pension payable as a series of monthly payments for at least the life of the
Participant.
Annuity Starting Date : The Annuity Starting Date shall be the first day of the first period for
which an amount is payable under this Plan as an annuity or in any other form. A Participant who: (1) is
reemployed after his initial Annuity Starting Date, and (2) is entitled to benefits hereunder after his
reemployment, shall have a subsequent Annuity Starting Date for such benefits only to the extent provided in
Section 6.3(b).
Cashout Limit : The annual dollar limit on elective deferrals under Code section 402(g)(1)(B), as
in effect from time to time.
Code : The Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended from time to time. All references herein
to particular Code Sections shall also refer to any successor provisions and shall include all related
regulations, interpretations and other guidance.
Company : PepsiCo, Inc., a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of
North Carolina or its successor or successors.
Covered Compensation : “Covered Compensation” as that term is defined in Part B of the
Salaried Plan.
Credited Service : The period of a Participant’ s employment, calculated in accordance with
Section 3.3, which is counted for purposes of determining the amount of benefits payable to, or on behalf of,
the Participant.
- 7 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramDisability Retirement Pension : The Retirement Pension available to a Participant under
Section 4.5.
Early 409A Retirement Pension : The 409A Retirement Pension available to a Participant under
Section 4.2.
Elapsed T ime Service : The period of time beginning with a Participant’ s first date of
employment with the PepsiCo Organization and ending with the Participant’ s Final Separation from Service,
irrespective of any breaks in service between those two dates. By way of illustration, if a Participant began
employment with the PepsiCo Organization on January 1, 2000, left the employment of the PepsiCo
Organization from January 1, 2001 until December 31, 2004, and was then reemployed by the PepsiCo
Organization on January 1, 2005 until he had a Final Separation from Service on December 31, 2008, the
Participant would have eight years of Elapsed T ime Service as of his Final Separation from Service.
Eligible Domestic Partner . The definition in this Section 2.1 is ef fective for applicable dates on
and after January 1, 2019, and applies solely to a Participant who is actively employed by , or on an Authorized
Leave of Absence from, a member of the PepsiCo Organization on or after January 1, 2019. For other dates or
Participants, see Appendix Article H.
(1) Definition . For applicable dates on or after January 1, 2019, “Eligible Domestic
Partner” means an individual who is of the same sex or opposite sex as the Participant and who
satisfies paragraph (a), (b) or (c), subject to the additional rules set forth in paragraph (e).
- 8 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(a) Civil Union . If on the applicable date the Participant has entered into a civil
union that is valid on the applicable date in the state in which it was entered into, the Participant’ s
Eligible Domestic Partner (if any) is the individual with whom the Participant has entered into such a
civil union.
(b) Enrollment in Health Benefits . If the Participant does not have an Eligible
Domestic Partner pursuant to paragraph (a) above, the Participant’ s Eligible Domestic Partner (if
any) is the individual who, on the applicable date, is enrolled in any of the Company’ s health benefit
options as the Participant’ s domestic partner .
(c) Other Acceptable Evidence of Partnership . If on the applicable date a
Participant does not have an Eligible Domestic Partner under paragraph (a) or (b) above, such
Participant’ s Eligible Domestic Partner (if any) is the individual who satisfies such criteria of domestic
partnership as the Plan Administrator has specified in writing.
(d) No Eligible Domestic Partner Except as Described Above . If on the
applicable date a Participant does not have an Eligible Domestic Partner under paragraph (a), (b), or
(c) above, such Participant is not eligible to have an Eligible Domestic Partner .
(e) Additional Rules . The term “Eligible Domestic Partner” does not apply to a
Participant’ s Eligible Spouse. A Participant is not permitted to have more than one Eligible Domestic
Partner at any point in
- 9 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programtime, and a Participant who has an Eligible Spouse is not permitted to have an Eligible Domestic
Partner .
(2) Terms Used in this Definition . For purposes of the definition of “Eligible Domestic
Partner” in this Section 2.1, the following definitions apply: “applicable date” means the earlier of the
Participant’ s Annuity Starting Date and date of death, and “state” means any domestic or foreign
jurisdiction having the legal authority to sanction civil unions .
Eligible Spouse : The spouse of a Participant to whom the Participant is considered lawfully
married for purposes of Federal tax law on the earlier of the Participant’ s Annuity Starting Date or the date of
the Participant’ s death and who, solely for periods before September 16, 2013, is of the opposite sex.
Employee : An individual who qualifies as an “Employee” as that term is defined in Part B of the
Salaried Plan.
Employer : An entity that qualifies as an “Employer” as that term is defined in Part B of the
Salaried Plan.
ERISA : Public Law No. 93-406, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, including
any amendments thereto, any similar subsequent federal laws, and any rules and regulations from time to time
in effect under any of such laws.
FICA Amount : The Participant’ s share of the Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) tax
imposed on the 409A Pension and Pre-409A Pension of the Participant under Code Sections 3101, 3121(a)
and 3121(v)(2).
- 10 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program409A Program : The program described in this document. The term “409A Program” is used to
identify the portion of the Plan that is subject to Section 409A.
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments : The guiding principles
as set forth in Common Appendix Article P AC to be applied by the Chair of the P AC when selecting the
members of the P AC.
Highest A verage Monthly Earnings : “Highest A verage Monthly Earnings” as that term is
defined in the Part B of the Salaried Plan, but without regard to the limitation imposed by section 401(a)(17) of
the Code (as such limitation is interpreted and applied under the Salaried Plan). Notwithstanding the foregoing,
to the extent that a Participant receives, during a leave of absence, earnings that would be counted as Highest
Average Monthly Earnings if they were received during a period of active service, but that will be received after
the Participant’ s Separation from Service, the Plan Administrator may provide for determining the Participant’ s
409A Pension at Separation from Service by projecting the benefit the Participant would have if all such
earnings were taken into account under the Plan.
Key Employee :
The individuals identified in accordance with the following paragraphs.
(1)    In General . Any Participant who at any time during the applicable year is:
(i)    An of ficer of any member of the PepsiCo Organization having annual
compensation greater than $130,000 (as adjusted for the applicable year under Code Section
416(i)(1));
- 11 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(ii)    A 5-percent owner of any member of the PepsiCo Organization; or
(iii)    A 1-percent owner of any member of the PepsiCo Organization having annual
compensation of more than $150,000.
For purposes of subparagraph (i) above, no more than 50 employees identified in the order of their
annual compensation shall be treated as of ficers. For purposes of this Section, annual compensation
means compensation as defined in T reas. Reg. §1.415(c)-2(a), without regard to T reas. Reg.
§§1.415(c)-2(d), 1.415(c)-2(e), and 1.415(c)-2(g). The Plan Administrator shall determine who is a Key
Employee in accordance with Code Section 416(i) (provided, that Code Section 416(i)(5) shall not apply
in making such determination), and provided further than the applicable year shall be determined in
accordance with Section 409A and that any modification of the foregoing definition that applies under
Section 409A shall be taken into account.
(2)    Applicable Y ear. Effective from and after December 31, 2007, the Plan Administrator
shall identify Key Employees as of the last day of each calendar year , based on compensation for such
year, and such designation shall be ef fective for purposes of this Plan for the twelve-month period
commencing on April 1  of the next following calendar year ( e.g., the Key Employee identification by
the Plan Administrator as of December 31, 2008 shall be ef fective for the period from April 1, 2009 to
March 31, 2010).
(3)    Rule of Administrative Convenience . Effective beginning with the December 31,
2017 identification date, in addition to the foregoing,st
- 12 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthe Plan Administrator shall treat all other employees classified as Leadership Group 6 and above on
the applicable identification date prescribed in paragraph (2) as Key Employees ef fective for the
twelve-month period commencing on April 1  of the next following calendar year (however , from the
April 1, 2008 ef fective date through February 25, 2010, Band IV and above applied in lieu of
Leadership Group 6 and above); provided that if this would result in counting more than 200 individuals
as Key Employees as of any such determination date, then the number treated as Key Employees will
be reduced to 200 by eliminating from consideration those employees otherwise added by this
paragraph (3) in order by their base compensation, from the lowest to the highest.
(4)    Identification of Key Employees Between February 26, 2010 and March 31, 2010 .
For the period between February 26, 2010 and March 31, 2010, Key Employees shall be identified by
combining the lists of Key Employees of all members of the PepsiCo Organization as in ef fect
immediately prior to February 26, 2010. The foregoing method of identifying Key Employees is
intended to comply with T reas. Reg. § 1.409A-1(i)(6)(i), which authorizes the use of an alternative
method of identifying specified employees that complies with T reas. Reg. §§ 1.409A-1(i)(5) and -1(i)(8)
and Section VII.C.4.d of the Preamble to the Final Regulations under Section 409A of the Code, which
permits “service recipients to simply combine the pre-transaction separate lists of specified employees
where it is determined that such treatment would be administratively less burdensome.”st
- 13 -

Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the 12-month periods beginning on the April 1, 2010 ef fective date
through March 31, 2018, Key Employees shall be identified as follows:
(i)    For the period that begins on April 1, 2010, and ends on March 31, 2011, an
employee shall be a Key Employee (subject to subparagraph (iii) below) if he was classified as at
least a Band IV or its equivalent on December 31, 2009. For this purpose, an employee shall be
considered to be at least a Band IV or its equivalent as of a date if the employee is classified as
one of the following types of employees in the PepsiCo Organization on that date: (i) a Band IV
employee or above in a PepsiCo Business, (ii) a Level E7 employee or above in a PBG
Business, or (iii) a Salary Grade 19 employee or above at a P AS Business.
(ii)    For the twelve-month period that begins on April 1, 2011, and for each twelve-
month period that begins on April 1 in subsequent years through March 31, 2017, an employee
shall be a Key Employee (subject to subparagraph (iii) below) if the employee was an employee
of the PepsiCo Organization who was classified as Band IV or above on the December 31 that
immediately precedes such April 1.
(iii)    For the period covered by this paragraph (5) notwithstanding the rule of
administrative convenience in paragraph (3) above, an employee shall be a Key Employee for
the 12-month period that begins on any April 1, if as of the preceding December 31 the
- 14 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programemployee would be a specified employee, within the meaning of T reasury Regulation 1.409A-
1(i), or any successor , by applying as of such December 31 the default rules that apply under
such regulation for determining the minimum number of a service recipient’ s specified
employees. If the preceding sentence and the methods for identifying Key Employees set forth in
subparagraph (i) or (ii) above, taken together , would result in more than 200 individuals being
counted as Key Employees as of any December 31 determination date, then the number of
individuals treated as Key Employees pursuant to subparagraph (i) or (ii), who are not described

(iv)    For purposes of this paragraph (5), “P AS Business” means each employer ,
division of an employer or other organizational subdivision of an employer that the Company
classifies as part of the P AS business; “PBG Business” means each employer , division of an
employer or other organizational subdivision of an employer that the Company classifies as part
of the PBG business; and “PepsiCo Business” means each employer , division of an employer or
other organizational subdivision of an employer that the Company classifies as part of the
PepsiCo business.
The method for identifying Key Employees set forth in this definition is intended as an alternative method of
identifying Key Employees under T reas. Reg. § 1.409A-1(i)(5), and
- 15 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programis adopted herein and shall be interpreted and applied consistently with the rules applicable to such alternative
arrangements.
Late 409A Retirement Pension : The 409A Retirement Pension available to a Participant under
Section 4.4.
Late Retirement Date : The Late Retirement Date shall be the first day of the month coincident
with or immediately following a Participant’ s actual Retirement Date occurring after his Normal Retirement
Age.
Normal 409A Retirement Pension : The Retirement Pension available to a Participant under
Section 4.1.
Normal Retirement Age : The Normal Retirement Age under the Plan is age 65 or , if later , the
age at which a Participant first has 5 Y ears of Elapsed T ime Service.
Normal Retirement Date : A Participant’ s Normal Retirement Date shall be the first day of the
month coincident with or immediately following a Participant’ s Normal Retirement Age.
Participant : An Employee participating in the Plan in accordance with the provisions of
Section 3.1.
Pension : One or more payments that are payable by the Plan to a person who is entitled to
receive benefits under the Plan. The term “409A Pension” shall be used to refer to the portion of a Pension
that is derived from the 409A Program. The term “Pre-409A Pension” shall be used to refer to the portion of a
Pension that is derived from the Pre-409A Program.
- 16 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramPepsiCo Administration Committee or P AC: The committee that has the responsibility for the
administration and operation of the Plan, as set forth in the Plan, as well as any other duties set forth therein. 
As of any time, the Chair of the P AC shall be the person who is then the Company’ s Senior V ice President,
Total Rewards, but if such position is vacant or eliminated, the Chair shall be the person who is acting to fulfill
the majority of the duties of the position (or plurality of the duties, if no one is fulfilling a majority), as such
duties existed immediately prior to the vacancy or the position elimination.  The Chair shall appoint the other
members of the P AC, applying the principles set forth in the Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan
Committee Appointments and acting promptly from time to time to ensure that there are four other members of
the P AC, each of whom shall have experience and expertise relevant to the responsibilities of the P AC.  At
least two times each year , the P AC shall prepare a written report of its significant activities that shall be
available to any U.S.-based executive of the Company who is at least a senior vice president. 
PepsiCo Organization : The controlled group of organizations of which the Company is a part,
as defined by Code section 414 and regulations issued thereunder . An entity shall be considered a member of
the PepsiCo Organization only during the period it is one of the group of organizations described in the
preceding sentence.
Plan : The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan, the Plan set forth herein and in the Pre-409A
Program document(s), as the Plan may be amended from time to time (subject to the limitations on
amendment that are applicable hereunder and under
- 17 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthe Pre-409A Program). The Plan is also sometimes referred to as PEP , or as the PepsiCo Pension Benefit
Equalization Plan.
Plan Administrator : The P AC, or its delegate or delegates. The Plan Administrator shall have
authority to administer the Plan as provided in Article VII.
Plan Y ear: The 12-month period commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31.
Pre-409A Program : The portion of the Plan that governs deferrals that are not subject to Section
409A. The terms of the Pre-409A Program are set forth in a separate document (or separate set of
documents).
Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension : The Pension available to an Eligible Domestic
Partner under the Plan. The term “Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension” shall be used to refer to
the Pension available to an Eligible Domestic Partner under Section 4.12 of this document.
Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension : The Pension available to an Eligible Spouse under the
Plan. The term “Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension” shall be used to refer to the Pension available to an
Eligible Spouse under Section 4.6 of this document.
Primary Social Security Amount : In determining Pension amounts, Primary Social Security
Amount shall mean:
(1)    For purposes of determining the amount of a Retirement, V ested, Pre-Retirement
Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension, the Primary Social Security Amount
shall be the estimated monthly amount that may be payable to a Participant commencing at age 65 as
an old-
- 18 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programage insurance benefit under the provisions of T itle II of the Social Security Act, as amended. Such
estimates of the old-age insurance benefit to which a Participant would be entitled at age 65 shall be
based upon the following assumptions:
(i)    That the Participant’ s social security wages in any year prior to Retirement or
Separation from Service are equal to the T axable W age Base in such year , and
(ii)    That he will not receive any social security wages after Retirement or
Separation from Service.
However , in computing a V ested Pension under Formula A of Section 5.2, the estimate of the old-age
insurance benefit to which a Participant would be entitled at age 65 shall be based upon the assumption
that he continued to receive social security wages until age 65 at the same rate as the T axable W age
Base in ef fect at his Separation from Service. For purposes of this subsection, “social security wages”
shall mean wages within the meaning of the Social Security Act.
(2)    For purposes of determining the amount of a Disability Pension, the Primary Social
Security Amount shall be (except as provided in the next sentence) the initial monthly amount actually
received by the disabled Participant as a disability insurance benefit under the provisions of T itle II of
the Social Security Act, as amended and in ef fect at the time of the Participant’ s Retirement due to
disability . Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, for any period that a Participant receives a
Disability Pension before receiving a
- 19 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programdisability insurance benefit under the provisions of T itle II of the Social Security Act, then the
Participant’ s Primary Social Security Amount for such period shall be determined pursuant to
paragraph (1) above.
(3)    For purposes of paragraphs (1) and (2), the Primary Social Security Amount shall
exclude amounts that may be available because of the spouse or any dependent of the Participant or
any amounts payable on account of the Participant’ s death. Estimates of Primary Social Security
Amounts shall be made on the basis of the Social Security Act as in ef fect at the Participant’ s
Separation from Service, without regard to any increases in the social security wage base or benefit
levels provided by such Act which take ef fect thereafter .
Prohibited Misconduct : Any of the following activities engaged in, directly or indirectly , by a
Participant shall constitute Prohibited Misconduct:
(1)    The Participant accepting any employment, assignment, position or responsibility , or
acquiring any ownership interest, which involves the Participant’ s “Participation” (as defined below) in a
business entity that markets, sells, distributes or produces “Covered Products” (as defined below),
unless such business entity makes retail sales or consumes Covered Products without in any way
competing with the PepsiCo Organization.
(2)    The Participant, directly or indirectly (including through someone else acting on the
Participant’ s recommendation, suggestion, identification or advice), soliciting any PepsiCo Organization
employee to leave the PepsiCo Organization’ s employment or to accept any position with any other
entity .
- 20 -
