summary:
- Scope: Excerpts from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program covering Article III (Participation and Service) and part of Article IV (Requirements for Benefits).

- Participation (Art. III, Sec. 3.1):
  - An employee is a Participant during any period when they would currently be entitled to a Pension under the Plan, or would be but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
  - Entitlement can later cease.
  - All eligibility exclusions from the Salaried Plan apply.

- Service rules (Sec. 3.2):
  - Eligibility for a Pension or, if death occurs before benefits start, a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension, is based on Service as defined in Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Inpats: Provisions that disregard pre-transfer Service for certain inbound transfers to the U.S. do not apply to this Plan before Jan 1, 2015, unless needed to prevent benefit duplication.
  - Leaves of absence: If Service would extend past Separation due to a leave, the Plan Administrator may project benefits at Separation as if such Service were included.

- Credited Service (Sec. 3.3):
  - Pension and pre-retirement survivor benefits are based on Credited Service per Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Inpats: Rules that disregard pre-transfer Credited Service do not apply to individuals transferring before Oct 1, 2014, unless needed to avoid duplication with the Salaried Plan.
  - Leaves of absence: Similar projection authority at Separation for Credited Service.

- Requirements for Benefits (Art. IV):
  - General: Participants may receive a Pension; eligible surviving spouses or domestic partners may receive survivor benefits, with amounts determined under Article V.
  - Normal 409A Retirement Pension (Sec. 4.1): Separation after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
  - Early 409A Retirement Pension (Sec. 4.2): Separation before Normal Retirement Age, with at least age 55 and 10+ years of Elapsed Time Service.
  - 409A Vested Pension (Sec. 4.3): Available if vested under Section 4.7 and Separation occurs before Normal/Early eligibility; no benefit if vesting is not met.
  - Late 409A Retirement Pension (Sec. 4.4): No payments until Late Retirement Date for those working past Normal Retirement Age; amount determined under Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
text:
ARTICLE III
Participation and Service
3.1    Participation : An Employee shall be a Participant in the Plan during the period:
(a)    When he would be currently entitled to receive a Pension under the Plan if his employment
terminated at such time, or
(b)    When he would be so entitled but for the vesting requirement of Section 4.7.
It is expressly contemplated that an Employee, who is entitled to receive a Pension under the Plan as of a particular
time, may subsequently cease to be entitled to receive a Pension under the Plan. An individual’ s entitlement to
receive a Pension under the Plan is subject to all exclusions from eligibility that apply under the Salaried Plan and,
therefore, all such exclusions shall be given ef fect in determining eligibility under the Plan.
3.2    Service : A Participant’ s entitlement to a Pension or , in the event the Participant dies before
commencing a benefit hereunder , either a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension for his Eligible Spouse or a Pre-
Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension for his Eligible Domestic Partner , shall be determined under Article IV based
upon his period of Service. A Participant’ s period of Service shall be determined under Article III of Part B of the
Salaried Plan, except as provided in (a) below .
(a) Inpats. Any Salaried Plan provision which results in disregarding for certain purposes the pre-
transfer Service of certain inpats who transfer to the United States, shall not
- 29 -

(b)    Leaves of Absence . If a Participant’ s period of Service (as so determined) would extend beyond
the Participant’ s Separation from Service date because of a leave of absence, the Plan Administrator may provide for
determining the Participant’ s 409A Pension at Separation from Service by projecting the benefit the Participant would
have if all such Service were taken into account under the Plan.
3.3    Credited Service : Subject to the next two sentences, the amount of a Participant’ s Pension, Pre-
Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension shall be based upon the Participant’ s

(a)    Inpats . Any provision in Section 3.5 of Part B of the Salaried Plan which resulted in

apply under this Plan in the case of such inpats who transfer to the United States before October 1, 2014,
unless such earlier application avoids duplication of benefits under the Salaried Plan.
(b)    Leaves of Absence . If a Participant’ s period of Credited Service (as so determined) would
extend beyond the Participant’ s Separation from Service date because of a leave of absence, the Plan

projecting the benefit the Participant would have if all such Service were taken into account under the Plan.

A Participant shall be eligible to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible

summary:
- Scope: Article IV (Requirements for Benefits) and the start of Article V (Amount of Retirement Pension) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

- Eligibility for pensions:
  - Normal 409A Retirement Pension: payable upon separation from service at or after Normal Retirement Age.
  - Early 409A Retirement Pension: payable upon separation before Normal Retirement Age after at least age 55 and 10+ years of Elapsed Time Service.
  - 409A Vested Pension: payable if vested under Section 4.7 and separated before qualifying for Normal/Early; no benefit if vesting not met.
  - Late 409A Retirement Pension: for those working past Normal Retirement Age; payments begin at Late Retirement Date and are determined by Part B of the Salaried Plan with specified exceptions.
  - 409A Disability Pension: available if the Salaried Plan disability criteria are met; split into Pre-Separation Accruals and Post-LTD Accruals (to the earlier of age 65, Salaried Plan benefit commencement, or recovery).

- Survivor benefits before retirement:
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: payable if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date; starts the month after the later of death or the date the participant would have turned 55; amount determined under Section 5.3 (after applying Section 5.6). For vested terminated employees, the participant’s benefit is reduced by an age-based annual charge for each year spouse coverage is in effect; no reduction for coverage within 90 days after termination.
  - Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension: similar structure and commencement; amounts under Section 5.8 (after Section 5.6). For vested terminated employees, participant’s benefit is reduced by an age-based annual charge; no reduction for coverage within 180 days after termination.

- Vesting: Full vesting in the 409A Accrued Benefit occurs when fully vested under Part B of the Salaried Plan (subject to Section 8.7 related to Code section 457A).

- Time of payment and interest: 409A Pension distributions commence per Section 6.1 (subject to Section 6.6). Any interest due to delayed payment (per Salaried Plan rules) accrues under the 409A Program and is paid with the 409A Pension, but no interest is paid if the delay is participant-caused or prohibited by IRS 409A correction guidance.

- Small-balance cashouts (limited cashouts under Treas. Reg. 1.409A-3(j)(4)(v)):
  - Participant, spouse, and domestic partner 409A pensions may be automatically cashed out in a lump sum if the actuarial present value is at or below the Plan’s Cashout Limit (historically $15,000 before December 1, 2012).
  - Special discretionary cashouts of 409A Vested Pensions may be made by the Plan Administrator on specified dates (e.g., December 1, 2012, and later designated months), with written lists documenting selections.
  - All 409A nonaccount balance benefits across applicable plans must be cashed out together if the limit is met; cashouts respect any required six-month delay; no participant or survivor election is permitted.
  - Cashouts are not available effective January 1, 2018, for participants eligible for certain “Kicker” benefits under a Severance Program (as defined in Appendix Article E).

- Reemployment: If a retiree receiving an annuity is rehired and re-eligible under the Salaried Plan, existing annuity payments continue unchanged; any new 409A accruals are paid after the subsequent separation.

- Forfeiture for misconduct: Post-2008 Accruals are forfeited (and recoverable if already paid) if the participant engages in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of separation.

- Article V—Amount of Retirement Pension (overview and formula):
  - When payable, the 409A Pension is determined under Sections 5.1 or 5.3, subject to adjustments (e.g., 4.6(b), 5.4) and the Plan freeze in Article I.
  - Section 5.1 formula: 409A Pension equals Total Pension minus the Salaried Plan Pension minus the Pre-409A Pension (not below zero), calculated with appropriate early/late commencement adjustments, relative value of forms, actuarial equivalence, and anti-duplication rules as administered by the Plan Administrator.

ARTICLE IV
Requirements for Benefits
A Participant shall be eligible to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible
Domestic Partner , as applicable, shall be eligible for certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article. The amount
of any such Pension or survivor benefit shall be determined in accordance with Article V .
4.1    Normal 409A Retirement Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for a Normal 409A Retirement
Pension if he Separates from Service after attaining Normal Retirement Age.
4.2    Early 409A Retirement Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for an Early 409A Retirement
Pension if he Separates from Service prior to attaining Normal Retirement Age but after attaining at least age 55 and
completing 10 or more years of Elapsed T ime Service.
4.3    409A V ested Pension : A Participant who is vested under Section 4.7 shall be eligible to receive a
409A V ested Pension if he Separates from Service before he is eligible for a Normal 409A Retirement Pension or an
Early 409A Retirement Pension. A Participant who terminates employment prior to satisfying the vesting requirement
in Section 4.7 shall not be eligible to receive a Pension under this Plan.
4.4    Late 409A Retirement Pension : A Participant who continues without a Separation from Service
after his Normal Retirement Age shall not receive a Pension until his Late Retirement Date. Thereafter , a Participant
shall be eligible for a Late Retirement Pension determined in accordance with Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried
Plan (but without regard to

Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan).
4.5    409A Disability Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for a 409A Disability Pension if he meets
the requirements for a Disability Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan. A Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension, if
any, shall generally be comprised of two parts. The first part shall represent the benefits with respect to a disabled
Participant’ s Credited Service through the day of the Participant’ s Separation from Service ( i.e., the Participant’ s “Pre-
Separation Accruals”). In the event the disabled Participant continues to receive Credited Service related to the
disability after such Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension shall have a second part,
which shall represent all benefits accrued with respect to Credited Service from the date immediately following the
Participant’ s Separation from Service until the earliest of the Participant’ s (i) attainment of age 65, (ii) benefit
commencement date under Part B of the Salaried Plan or (iii) recovery from the disability ( i.e., the Participant’ s “Post-
LTD Accruals”).
4.6    Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension : A Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension is payable
under this section only in the event the Participant dies prior to his Annuity Starting Date. Any Pre-Retirement

to Section 4.9, any Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension shall continue monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse.

summary:
- Scope: Article V sets how 409A retirement and pre-retirement survivor pensions are calculated under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) – 409A Program, including definitions, coordination with the Salaried Plan and Pre‑409A Program, the PEP Guarantee, adjustments, offsets, and exclusions. Article VI begins the rules for distribution timing and form.

- Core 409A Pension calculation (Section 5.1):
  - Participant’s 409A Pension = Total Pension − Salaried Plan Pension − Pre‑409A Pension (not below zero).
  - Determined with early/late commencement adjustments as of the Annuity Starting Date, relative value of elected forms of payment, actuarial equivalence, and rules to prevent duplication considering prior payments.
  - For Annuity Starting Dates after 12/31/2018, may “make up” harsher early retirement reductions applied to the Pre‑409A Pension compared to 2019 Salaried Plan Factors.
  - Total Pension = greater of (i) Part B Salaried Plan pension ignoring Code 401(a)(17)/415 limits and the post‑NRD actuarial increase under Part B §5.7(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee; comparisons reflect relative value of forms.

- PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2):
  - Eligibility: 1988 pensionable earnings with an Employer ≥ $75,000 (as defined under the 1988 Salaried Plan; excludes earnings from non‑Employer entities at the time).
  - Benefit formulas:
    - Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service (CS) + 1% of HAME for CS >10 − 1⅔% of Primary Social Security Amount (PSSA) × CS (max 30). Vested Pension is prorated based on actual vs. projected CS to Normal Retirement Age (NRA).
    - Formula B (for classifications eligible before 7/1/1975): greater of (A) 1½% of HAME × CS − 50% of PSSA, or (B) 3% of HAME × CS up to 15 − 50% of PSSA. Disability pensions use CS and pay bases at disability per Salaried Plan.
  - Survivor benefit for Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner: 50% of Participant’s annuity with no reduction to the Participant; if survivor is >10 years younger, reduce 0.8% per year for years 11–20 younger and 0.4% per year thereafter.
  - Additional reductions/adjustments:
    - Early retirement: 0.25% (3/12 of 1%) per month before NRA.
    - Vested Pension commencing before NRA: actuarial equivalent; apply pre‑retirement spouse/domestic partner coverage reductions.
    - If elected form provides greater survivor benefit, or a non‑spouse survivor, or includes inflation protection, reduce to actuarial equivalence of the standard benchmark form.
  - Lump sum: actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, including survivor and early‑retirement adjustments; actuarial equivalence preserves pre‑1989 plan value and complies with Section 409A’s annuity equivalence rules.

- Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension (Section 5.3):
  - Amount = Total PR Spouse’s Pension − Salaried Plan PR Spouse’s Pension − PR Spouse’s Pension from Pre‑409A Program (not below zero).
  - Uses early/late commencement adjustments and actuarial equivalence; considers timing/form of any prior payments.
  - Total PR Spouse’s Pension = greater of the Salaried Plan amount ignoring Code limits and Part B §5.7(d), or the PEP Guarantee PR Spouse’s Pension; comparison done at Participant’s NRA and then adjusted for actual commencement.
  - PEP Guarantee PR Spouse’s Pension: equal to survivor benefit under a QJSA assuming separation and commencement aligned with survivor benefit start, and death the day after; special minimum for active/disabled Participants = 25% of PEP Guarantee, with CS and pay bases as of death; no early commencement reduction. Applies principles parallel to §5.1(b) and the actuarial‑equivalence sentence in §5.2(b)(2).

- Certain adjustments (Section 5.4):
  - Rehired Participants: if Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated for added CS, recalculate PEP benefits to the extent permitted under Section 409A; adjust PEP Guarantee for in‑service/prior distributions consistent with Salaried Plan, considering this Plan and any “specified plans.”
  - Increases under other specified plans: if a court/administrator/other increases a related plan benefit after PEP is determined, recalculate PEP (subject to 409A) and recover any overpayment; avoid duplication with Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified plans.
  - No offsets that violate Section 409A: apply Salaried Plan non‑duplication/transfer rules to Total Pension only if they do not change 409A time/form; Company will seek compliant special arrangements under the other plan to avoid prohibited changes.

- Excludable employment (Section 5.5): Executives who sign agreements waiving eligibility or participation will not accrue or increase benefits for that employment; applies to agreements on/after 1/1/2009, whether signed before or after eligibility/participation.

- Pre‑409A Pension (Section 5.6): The grandfathered portion under Treas. Reg. §1.409A‑6(a)(3)(i),(iv); determined using principles akin to §5.1(b) and the actuarial‑equivalence standard in §5.2(b)(2).

- Offsets (Section 5.7):
  - Company may offset benefits by amounts the Participant owes the Company (incurred during employment), within 409A annual limits, and at the same time/amount as the debt would be due.
  - When a Prior 409A Benefit exists, compute any additional 409A Benefit net of an actuarially equivalent offset reflecting early/late commencement and form values; example: Post‑Disability Accruals offset by Pre‑Separation Accruals.

- Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Section 5.8):
  - Structure mirrors the spouse provisions: Amount = Total PR Domestic Partner’s Pension − Salaried Plan PR Domestic Partner’s Pension − Pre‑409A Program portion (not below zero); apply early/late and actuarial equivalence.
  - Total PR Domestic Partner’s Pension: greater of Salaried Plan amount ignoring Code limits and Part B §5.7(d), or PEP Guarantee PR Domestic Partner’s amount; compare at Participant’s NRA then adjust for commencement.
  - PEP Guarantee PR Domestic Partner’s Pension: QJSA‑based survivor model; special minimum for active/disabled = 25% of PEP Guarantee; no early commencement reduction; same actuarial‑equivalence principles apply.

- Distributions (Article VI introduction and §6.1 start):
  - Article VI governs distribution of 409A Pensions to Participants and any beneficiary continuation; Pre‑Retirement Spouse/Domestic Partner pensions are paid as life annuities (subject to cashout rules in §4.9); Pre‑409A Pension distributions follow Pre‑409A Program terms.
  - 409A Retirement Pension form/timing (§6.1):
    - Default: Single lump sum on the first day of the month on/after the Retirement Date, subject to key‑employee delay (§6.6).
    - Prior elections: If a compliant election was made by 12/31/2007 at least six months before and in a calendar year prior to the Annuity Starting Date, distributions follow that election.

ARTICLE V
Amount of Retirement Pension
When a 409A Pension becomes payable to or on behalf of a Participant under this Plan, the amount of
such 409A Pension shall be determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever is applicable), subject to any
adjustments required under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4 and subject to the freeze of the Plan described in Article I.
5.1    Participant’ s 409A Pension : Subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A), a Participant’ s 409A Pension
shall be determined as follows –
(a)    Calculating the 409A Pension : A Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be calculated as follows
(on the basis specified in subsection (b) below and using the definitions appearing in subsection (c) below):
(1)    His T otal Pension, reduced by
(2)    His Salaried Plan Pension, and then further reduced by  (but not below zero)
(3)    His Pre-409A Pension.
(b)    Basis for Determining : The 409A Pension amount in subsection (a) above shall be
determined on a basis that (i) takes into account applicable reductions for early or late commencement as of
the Annuity Starting Date of the 409A Pension, (ii) reflects, if applicable and customary , the relative value of
forms of payment, and (iii) otherwise adjusts the reductions in (a)(2) and (3) above to their Actuarial
Equivalent, in each such respect as appropriate and customary under the circumstances and in accordance
with rules authorized by the Plan Administrator , including to take account the time and form of any prior
payments and to eliminate all duplication of benefits as
- 41 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programdetermined by the Plan Administrator , and (iii) ef fective for Annuity Starting Dates after December 31, 2018,
allows a Participant’ s 409A Pension to provide a makeup (as appropriate under the circumstances under rules
authorized by the Plan Administrator) for the application of early commencement reduction factors to the
Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension that apply a greater early commencement reduction to such Pre-409A Pension
than would apply under the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors (including with respect to any portion of the
Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension that is derived from the PEP Guarantee).
(c)    Definitions : The following definitions apply for purposes of this section.
(1)    A Participant’ s “Total Pension” means the greater of:
(i)    The amount of the Participant’ s pension determined under the terms of Part B
of the Salaried Plan, but without regard to: (A) the limitations imposed by sections 401(a)(17) and
415 of the Code (as such limitations are interpreted and applied under the Salaried Plan), and
(B) the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan (relating to
benefits that are deferred beyond the Participant’ s Normal Retirement Date); or
(ii)    The amount (if any) of the Participant’ s PEP Guarantee determined under
Section 5.2.
As necessary to ensure the Participant’ s receipt of a “greater of” benefit, the foregoing comparison shall
be made by reflecting, as applicable, the relative value of forms of payment.
- 42 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(2)    A Participant’ s “Salaried Plan Pension” means the amount of the Participant’ s
pension determined under the terms of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
(3)    A Participant’ s “Pre-409A Pension” means the amount of the Participant’ s pension
determined under Section 5.6.
5.2    PEP Guarantee : A Participant who is eligible under subsection (a) below shall be entitled to a PEP
Guarantee benefit determined under subsection (b) below . In the case of other Participants, the PEP Guarantee shall
not apply .
(a)    Eligibility : A Participant shall be covered by this section if the Participant has 1988
pensionable earnings from an Employer of at least $75,000. For purposes of this section, “1988 pensionable
earnings” means the Participant’ s remuneration for the 1988 calendar year , within the meaning of the Salaried
Plan as in ef fect in 1988. “1988 pensionable earnings” does not include remuneration from an entity
attributable to any period when that entity was not an Employer .
(b)    PEP Guarantee Formula : The amount of a Participant’ s PEP Guarantee shall be
determined under the applicable formula in paragraph (1), subject to the special rules in paragraph (2).
(1)    Formulas : The amount of a Participant’ s Pension under this paragraph shall be
determined in accordance with subparagraph (i) below . However , if the Participant was actively
employed by the PepsiCo Organization in a classification eligible for the Salaried Plan prior to July 1,
1975, the amount of his Pension under this paragraph shall be the greater of the amounts
- 43 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programdetermined under subparagraphs (i) and (ii), provided that subparagraph (ii)(B) shall not apply in
determining the amount of a V ested Pension.
(i)    Formula A : The Pension amount under this subparagraph shall be:
(A)    3 percent of the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings for the
first 10 years of Credited Service, plus
(B)    1 percent of the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings for
each year of Credited Service in excess of 10 years, less
(C)    1-2/3 percent of the Participant’ s Primary Social Security Amount
multiplied by years of Credited Service not in excess of 30 years.
In determining the amount of a V ested Pension under this Formula A, the Pension shall first be
calculated on the basis of (I) the Credited Service the Participant would have earned had he
remained in the employ of the Employer until his Normal Retirement Age, and (II) his Highest
Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at his Separation from Service,
and then shall be reduced by multiplying the resulting amount by a fraction, the numerator of
which is the Participant’ s actual years of Credited Service on his Separation from Service and the
denominator of which is the years of Credited Service he would have
- 44 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programearned had he remained in the employ of an Employer until his Normal Retirement Age.
(ii)    Formula B : The Pension amount under this subparagraph shall be the greater
of (A) or (B) below:
(A)    1-1/2 percent of Highest A verage Monthly Earnings times the number
of years of Credited Service, less 50 percent of the Participant’ s Primary Social Security
Amount, or
(B)    3 percent of Highest A verage Monthly Earnings times the number of
years of Credited Service up to 15 years, less 50 percent of the Participant’ s Primary
Social Security Amount.
In determining the amount of a Disability Pension under Formula A or B above, the Pension shall be
calculated on the basis of the Participant’ s Credited Service (determined in accordance with
Section 3.3(c)(3) of Part B of the Salaried Plan), and his Highest A verage Monthly Earnings and
Primary Social Security Amount at the date of disability .
(2)    Calculation : The amount of the PEP Guarantee shall be determined pursuant to
paragraph (1) above, subject to the following special rules:
(i)    Surviving Eligible Spouse’ s or Eligible Domestic Partner ’s Annuity :    Subject to
subparagraph (iii) below and the last sentence of this subparagraph, if the Participant has an
Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , the Participant’ s Eligible Spouse or Eligible
- 45 -

begin on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’ s death and shall

such Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner shall be reduced by an additional 0.4
percent.
(ii)    Reductions : The following reductions shall apply in determining a Participant’ s
PEP Guarantee.

amount shall be reduced by 3/12ths of 1 percent for each month by which the benefit
commencement date precedes the date the Participant would attain his Normal

(B)    If the Participant is entitled to a V ested Pension, the payment amount

(C)    This clause applies if the Participant will receive his Pension in a form

(D)    This clause applies if the Participant will receive his Pension in a form
that provides a survivor annuity for a
- 47 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programbeneficiary who is not his Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner . In this instance,
the Participant’ s Pension under this section shall be reduced so that the total value of the

(E)    This clause applies if the Participant will receive his Pension in an
Annuity form that includes inflation protection described in Section 6.2(b). In this instance,

(iii)    Lump Sum Conversion : The amount of the Retirement Pension determined

and survivor annuities in T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(b)(ii)(C)).
5.3    Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension : The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement

(2)    The Eligible Spouse’ s Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension, and then

(c)    Definitions : The following definitions apply for purposes of this section.

determined under the terms of Part B of the Salaried Plan, but without regard to: (A) the

title: Form and Timing of Distributions
heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions :
start_phrase: Benefits under the 409A Program shall be distributed as follows:
summary:
- Scope: Article VI governs distribution of benefits under the 409A Program when a participant becomes entitled to a pension and outlines continuation of benefits to beneficiaries after a participant’s death. Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s pensions are paid as lifetime annuities (subject to cashout rules). Pre‑409A benefits are governed by the Pre‑409A Program.
- 409A Retirement Pension (Form and Timing):
  - Default: Single lump sum payable on the first day of the month coincident with or next following the Retirement Date, subject to a delay for Key Employees (Section 6.6).
  - Prior payment elections: If made by December 31, 2007 and at least six months earlier in a prior calendar year than the Annuity Starting Date, the election controls. Elections could (i) choose an annuity form, (ii) change commencement timing, or both. Elections by participants eligible only for a Vested Pension at separation are disregarded.
  - Default annuity forms when an annuity is elected: Qualified Joint & Survivor Annuity (QJSA) if married; Single Life Annuity if unmarried, unless an optional form is elected under Section 6.2 following procedures in Section 6.3(a). Marital status is determined on the Annuity Starting Date.
  - If commencement is delayed by election, the benefit is increased for interest at the plan’s actuarial lump-sum rate through the payment processing date; interest is paid at the participant’s elected time.
- 409A Vested Pension (Form and Timing), subject to cashouts (Section 4.9), key employee delay (Section 6.6), and Disability rules (6.1(c)):
  - Separation before age 55 with at least 5 years of Service: Annuity commences on/after age 55 (first day of the coincident/next month). Default form is QJSA if married; Single Life if unmarried. An unmarried participant with an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% or 75% Survivor Annuity for the partner (per Section 6.2). Marital/partner status determined at the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Separation at ages 55–64 with at least 5 but less than 10 years of Service: Annuity commences the first of the month following Separation from Service, with forms as above and optional forms available under Section 6.2 via Section 6.3(a) procedures.
- 409A Disability Pension:
  - Pre‑Separation Accruals: Paid the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; forms available are those for Vested or Retirement Pensions under Section 6.2 (varying by marital/domestic partner status).
  - Post‑LTD Accruals: Paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following attainment of age 65.
- Available Forms of Payment (Section 6.2):
  - Applies to participants entitled to a Retirement Pension under 6.1(a)(2) or a Vested Pension under 6.1(b).
  - Retirement Pension: Participant may choose among optional forms by valid election under Section 6.3(a).
  - Vested Pension:
    - If married on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect only certain specified optional forms (referenced as paragraphs (1), (2)(ii), (2)(iii)) with the Eligible Spouse as beneficiary.
    - If unmarried with an Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect designated survivor annuity options for the partner (text continues beyond the excerpt).
- Cross-references and conditions: Cashout distributions (Section 4.9), election procedures (Section 6.3(a)), key employee payment delay (Section 6.6), and definitions including Pre‑Separation Accruals and Post‑LTD Accruals (Section 4.5).
text:
1    Form and T iming of Distributions : Benefits under the 409A Program shall be distributed as follows:
(a)    409A Retirement Pension : The following rules govern the distribution of a Participant’ s
409A Retirement Pension:
(1)    Generally : A Participant’ s 409A Retirement Pension shall be distributed as a Single
Lump Sum on the first day of the month that is coincident with or next follows the Participant’ s
Retirement Date, subject to paragraph (2) and Section 6.6 (delay for Key Employees).
(2)    Prior Payment Election : Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a Participant who is entitled
to a 409A Retirement Pension and who made an election (i) up to and including December 31, 2007,
and (ii) at least six months prior to and in a calendar year prior to the Participant’ s Annuity Starting
Date shall receive his benefit in accordance with such payment election. A payment election allowed a
Participant to choose either (i) to receive a distribution of his
- 59 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programbenefit in an Annuity form, (ii) to commence distribution of his benefit at a time other than as provided
in paragraph 6.1(a)(1), or both (i) and (ii). A payment election made by a Participant who is only eligible
to receive a V ested Pension on his Separation from Service shall be disregarded. Subject to Section
4.9 (cashouts), a Participant who has validly elected to receive an Annuity shall receive his benefit as a
Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if he is married or as a Single Life Annuity if he is unmarried,
unless he elects one of the optional forms of payment described in Section 6.2 in accordance with the
election procedures in Section 6.3(a). A Participant shall be considered married if he is married on his
Annuity Starting Date (with such Annuity Starting Date determined taking into account any election
applicable under this subsection). To the extent a Participant’ s benefit commences later than it would
under paragraph 6.1(a)(1) as a result of an election under this paragraph 6.1(a)(2), the Participant’ s
benefit will be increased for earnings at the interest rate used to compute the Actuarial Equivalent lump
sum value through the date the check for payment is prepared, which interest shall be paid at the time
elected by the Participant under this paragraph 6.1(a)(2).
(b)    409A V ested Pension : Subject to Section 4.9, Section 6.6 and subsection (c) below , a
Participant’ s 409A V ested Pension shall be distributed in accordance with paragraph (1) or (2) below , unless,
in the case of a Participant who is married (as determined under the standards in paragraph 6.1(a)(2), above)
or has an Eligible Domestic Partner on his Annuity Starting Date, he elects one of the optional
- 60 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programforms of payment distributions in Section 6.2 in accordance with the election procedures in Section 6.3(a):
(1)    Separation Prior to Age 55: In the case of a Participant who Separates from Service
with at least five years of Service prior to attaining age 55, the Participant’ s 409A V ested Pension shall
be distributed as an Annuity commencing on the first of the month that is coincident with or
immediately follows the date he attains age 55, which shall be the Annuity Starting Date of his 409A
Vested Pension. A distribution under this subsection shall be in the form of a Qualified Joint and
Survivor Annuity if the Participant is married or as a Single Life Annuity if he is not married; provided
that an unmarried Participant who has an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% Survivor Annuity
or 75% Survivor Annuity with his Eligible Domestic Partner as his beneficiary as provided in Section
6.2. A Participant shall be considered married or to have an Eligible Domestic Partner for purposes of
this paragraph if he is married or has an Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date of his
409A V ested Pension.
(2)    Separation at Ages 55 Through 64 : In the case of a Participant who Separates from
Service with at least five years but less than ten years of Service and on or after attaining age 55 but
prior to attaining age 65, the Participant’ s 409A V ested Pension shall be distributed as an Annuity (as
provided in paragraph (1) above) commencing on the first of the month that follows his Separation from
Service.
- 61 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(c)    Disability Pension : The portion of a Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension representing Pre-
Separation Accruals shall be paid on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’ s
attainment of age 55 and (ii) the Participant’ s Separation from Service. The available forms of payment for the
portion of a Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension representing Pre-Separation Accruals (as defined in Section
4.5) shall be those forms available to a Participant who is entitled to a V ested Pension or a Retirement
Pension, as set forth in Section 6.2, below (including, to the extent applicable, the dif ferent forms available to a
married Participant / Participant with a domestic partner versus a single Participant). The portion of a
Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension representing Post-L TD Accruals shall be paid on the first day of the
month following the Participant’ s attainment of age 65 in a lump sum.

title: Available Forms of Payment
heading: 6.2 Available Forms of Payment :
start_phrase:
This section sets forth the payment options available to a Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension
under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) above or a V ested Pension under subsection 6.1(b) above.
summary:
- Defines Disability Pension payment timing under the 409A Program:
  - Pre-Separation Accruals are paid on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation from Service, using the same payment forms available for Vested or Retirement Pensions (including marital/domestic partner distinctions).
  - Post-Long-Term-Disability (Post-LTD) Accruals are paid in a lump sum on the first day of the month after the Participant turns 65.
- Sets out available annuity forms for Participants entitled to a Retirement Pension or a Vested Pension:
  - Retirement Pension: may elect from the full menu of options via proper election.
  - Vested Pension:
    - If married on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect Single Life Annuity, 75% Survivor, or 50% Survivor with Eligible Spouse as beneficiary; no other forms permitted.
    - If not married but has an Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect 75% Survivor or 50% Survivor with Eligible Domestic Partner as beneficiary; no other forms permitted.
    - If not married and no Eligible Domestic Partner: must receive a Single Life Annuity.
  - Optional annuity forms (each actuarially equivalent to a Single Life Annuity):
    - Single Life Annuity.
    - Survivor Options: 100%, 75%, or 50% (50% is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if beneficiary is an Eligible Spouse).
    - Ten Years Certain and Life.
- Provides optional inflation protection for annuity payments:
  - 5% or 7% protection: initial reduction to monthly benefit, with increases each year to the extent prior-year inflation exceeds the chosen threshold.
  - Adjustments apply each January 1, starting with the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date, based on inflation for the 12 months ending September 30, measured like Social Security COLAs.
  - Chosen inflation protection carries over to survivor benefits and is irrevocable.
- Establishes procedures for making Annuity Starting Date elections (Section 6.2), including special rules when there are multiple Annuity Starting Dates; defines the date an election is “received” as the postmark date or the actual receipt date by the Plan Administrator.

2    Available Forms of Payment : This section sets forth the payment options available to a Participant
who is entitled to a Retirement Pension under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) above or a V ested Pension under subsection
6.1(b) above.
(a)    Basic Forms : A Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension may choose one of the
following optional forms of payment by making a valid election in accordance with the election procedures in
Section 6.3(a). A Participant who is entitled to a V ested Pension and who is married on his Annuity Starting
Date may choose one of the optional forms of payment available under paragraph (1), (2)(ii) or (2)(iii) below
with his Eligible Spouse as his beneficiary (and no other optional form of payment available under this
subsection (a) shall be permitted to such a Participant). A Participant who is entitled to a V ested Pension, who
is not married and who has an Eligible Domestic Partner on his Annuity Starting Date may choose one of the
optional
- 62 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programforms available under paragraph (2)(ii) or (2)(iii) below with his Eligible Domestic Partner as his beneficiary
(and no other optional forms of payment available under this subsection shall be permitted to such a
Participant). A Participant who is entitled to a V ested Pension and who is not married and does not have an
Eligible Domestic Partner on his Annuity Starting Date shall receive a Single Life Annuity . Each optional
annuity is the actuarial equivalent of the Single Life Annuity:
(1)    Single Life Annuity Option : A Participant may receive his 409A Pension in the form
of a Single Life Annuity , which provides monthly payments ending with the last payment due prior to his
death.
(2)    Survivor Options : A Participant may receive his 409A Pension in accordance with
one of the following survivor options:
(i)    100 Percent Survivor Option : The Participant shall receive a reduced 409A
Pension payable for life, ending with the last monthly payment due prior to his death. Payments
in the same reduced amount shall continue after the Participant’ s death to his beneficiary for life,
beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’ s death and
ending with the last monthly payment due prior to the beneficiary’ s death.
(ii)    75 Percent Survivor Option : The Participant shall receive a reduced 409A
Pension payable for life, ending with the last monthly payment due prior to his death. Payments
in the amount of 75 percent of such reduced 409A Pension shall be continued after the
Participant’ s death to his beneficiary for life, beginning on the first day of
- 63 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthe month coincident with or following the Participant’ s death and ending with the last monthly
payment due prior to the beneficiary’ s death.
(iii)    50 Percent Survivor Option : The Participant shall receive a reduced 409A
Pension payable for life, ending with the last monthly payment due prior to his death. Payments
in the amount of 50 percent of such reduced 409A Pension shall be continued after the
Participant’ s death to his beneficiary for life, beginning on the first day of the month coincident
with or following the Participant’ s death and ending with the last monthly payment due prior to the
beneficiary’ s death. A 50 percent survivor option under this paragraph shall be a Qualified Joint
and Survivor Annuity if the Participant’ s beneficiary is his Eligible Spouse.
(iv)    Ten Years Certain and Life Option : The Participant shall receive a reduced
409A Pension which shall be payable monthly for his lifetime but for not less than 120 months. If
the retired Participant dies before 120 payments have been made, the monthly 409A Pension
amount shall be paid for the remainder of the 120 month period to the Participant’ s primary
beneficiary (or if the primary beneficiary has predeceased the Participant, the Participant’ s
contingent beneficiary).
(b)    Inflation Protection : The following levels of inflation protection may be provided to any
Participant who elects to receive all or a part of his 409A Retirement Pension as an Annuity:
- 64 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(1)    5 Percent Inflation Protection : A Participant’ s monthly benefit shall be initially
reduced, but thereafter shall be increased if inflation in the prior year exceeds 5 percent. The amount
of the increase shall be the dif ference between inflation in the prior year and 5 percent.
(2)    7 Percent Inflation Protection : A Participant’ s monthly benefit shall be initially
reduced, but thereafter shall be increased if inflation in the prior year exceeds 7 percent. The amount
of the increase shall be the dif ference between inflation in the prior year and 7 percent.
Benefits shall be subject to increase in accordance with this subsection each January 1, beginning with the
second January 1 following the Participant’ s Annuity Starting Date. The amount of inflation in the prior year
shall be determined based on inflation in the 12-month period ending on September 30 of such year , with
inflation measured in the same manner as applies on the Ef fective Date for adjusting Social Security benefits
for changes in the cost of living. Inflation protection that is in ef fect shall carry over to any survivor benefit
payable on behalf of a Participant, and shall increase the otherwise applicable survivor benefit as provided
above. Any election by a Participant to receive inflation protection shall be irrevocable by such Participant or
his surviving beneficiary .
6.

title: Procedures for Elections
heading: 6.3 Procedures for Elections :
start_phrase: This section sets forth the procedures for making Annuity Starting Date elections ( i.e., elections under Section 6.2).
summary:
- Describes two optional inflation-protection features for monthly annuity benefits:
  - 5% Inflation Protection: benefit is initially reduced; thereafter increased each January 1 by the excess of prior-year inflation over 5%.
  - 7% Inflation Protection: same mechanics, with a 7% threshold.
- Inflation adjustments begin on the second January 1 following the Participant’s Annuity Starting Date, based on inflation for the 12 months ending September 30, measured using the Social Security cost-of-living adjustment methodology in effect on the plan’s Effective Date.
- Elected inflation protection is irrevocable and carries over to increase any survivor benefit.

- Sets procedures for Annuity Starting Date elections (Section 6.3):
  - An election is deemed received if postmarked that day or actually received by close of business that day; spousal consent is not required.
  - Election of an optional annuity form (for a 409A Retirement Pension with a proper prior election or a 409A Vested Terminated Pension) must be in writing, signed, received at least one day before the Annuity Starting Date, specify an available optional form, and designate a beneficiary if applicable. Electronic elections/affirmations may be permitted.
  - For Participants with multiple Annuity Starting Dates (e.g., after rehire): initial elections continue to govern prior accruals; new elections at the subsequent Annuity Starting Date apply only to benefits accrued after rehire.
  - Marital status determination (effective Jan 1, 2014): default assumption is unmarried unless the Participant provides satisfactory notice before the Annuity Starting Date; the Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.

- Introduces special rules for survivor options (Section 6.4), including effects of certain deaths when an optional annuity with a survivor benefit has been elected (details partially shown).

title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
heading: 6.4 Special Rules for Survivor Options :
start_phrase: The following special rules shall apply for the survivor options available under Section 6.2.
summary:
- Addresses how elections at a subsequent Annuity Starting Date (after a rehire and subsequent Separation from Service) apply only to benefits accrued after rehire; prior unpaid accruals continue under the initial Annuity Starting Date elections.
- Establishes marital status determination rules (effective January 1, 2014): the Plan assumes a Participant is unmarried on the Annuity Starting Date unless the Participant provides satisfactory notice of marriage before that date; notice is given with the payment election or via Plan Administrator procedures; the Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.
- Sets special survivor option rules:
  - If a Participant or designated beneficiary dies before the Annuity Starting Date, any prior survivor annuity election is disregarded.
  - If the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date but before payments actually commence, the survivor election stands; survivor payments to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary begin the first day of the month after death; any owed back payments go to the Participant’s estate.
  - For the 120-payment certain option (Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)): if the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary before 120 payments are made, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate; if a beneficiary receiving payments dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
- Imposes age-difference limits when the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner:
  - 100% survivor option unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the Participant.
  - 75% survivor option unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger than the Participant.
- Introduces the next section on designation of beneficiary for forms of payment that include a survivor benefit.

heading: 6.5 Designation of Beneficiary :
start_phrase: A Participant who has elected under Section 6.2 to receive all or part of his Retirement Pension in a form of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a beneficiary who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
summary:
- Treatment of benefit elections upon death relative to the Annuity Starting Date: elections under certain options are disregarded if death occurs before the Annuity Starting Date; if death occurs after the Annuity Starting Date but before 409A Retirement Pension payments begin, the elected survivor form is honored, benefits start the first day of the month following death, and any back payments due go to the participant’s estate.

- Restrictions when the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner: the 100% survivor option is not permitted if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger; the 75% survivor option is not permitted if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger.
- Beneficiary designation rules for survivor options: beneficiaries must be designated on approved forms; for the 120-payments-certain option, both primary and contingent beneficiaries may be named; designations can be changed or revoked before the Annuity Starting Date and are effective only when filed with the Plan Administrator; if no beneficiary is properly designated for a survivor option, the default is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner; participants entitled only to a Vested Pension generally cannot name a beneficiary unless an optional form is elected, in which case the spouse/domestic partner is the beneficiary on the Annuity Starting Date.
- Required delay for Key Employees under Section 409A: for Key Employees, 409A Retirement Pension distributions begin on the earliest first day of a month at least six months after Separation from Service, or earlier upon death.

title: Administration
heading:
ARTICLE VII
Administration
start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate.
summary:
- Administration and authority:
  - The Plan Administrator has sole, absolute discretion to interpret the plan, issue regulations, keep records, and calculate benefits; its decisions are final and binding.
  - The Administrator may rely on participant-provided information (address, age, marital status).
  - Neither the Company nor the Administrator is a fiduciary; ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply.

- Facility of payment:
  - If a payee is incapacitated, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit; such payments fully discharge liability.

- Claims and appeals process:
  - The Administrator has exclusive authority over eligibility and benefit determinations; court review is under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard and limited to the administrative record.
  - Denial notices within 90 days (extendable to 180) must state reasons, cite plan provisions, list needed additional information, and describe review rights (including ERISA civil action).
  - Claimants have 60 days to seek review; decisions on review within 60 days (extendable to 120) with access to relevant documents at no charge.
  - Specific references to discretion do not limit the Administrator’s broader discretion.

- Mandatory exhaustion of remedies:
  - Claimants must fully exhaust plan claims procedures before filing in court; this requirement is intended to apply as broadly as possible.
  - Post-exhaustion litigation is limited to the administrative record.
  - The Administrator may establish special procedures (e.g., class claims) to facilitate exhaustion.
  - Definitions provided for Dispute, Claim (including interpretation, validity, administration, ERISA violations, benefit recovery, fiduciary breach, and related matters), and Claimant.
  - Examples clarify when exhaustion is not excused (e.g., inadequate claim submission or document requests).

- Limitations period and venue:
  - Two-year statute of limitations for claims, ERISA interference, and other actions, with accrual defined by earliest of specified events (e.g., receipt of calculation, identified payment date, knowledge of facts, first payment/denial).
  - Appeals correspondence does not toll the limitations period.
  - Exclusive venue: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York for claims filed on/after January 1, 2011.

- Miscellaneous:
  - No guarantee of employment; employers retain at-will termination rights.
  - Anti-alienation: benefits may not be assigned, pledged, garnished, or transferred (including in divorce/child support contexts); attempts are void and not binding on the Company.
  - Unfunded status: obligations are payable from the Company’s general assets; participants are unsecured general creditors.
  - Company action under the plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or the Compensation Committee (section truncated).

ARTICLE VII
Administration
7.1    Authority to Administer Plan : The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have
the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate. The Plan Administrator shall
maintain Plan records and make benefit calculations, and may rely upon information furnished it by the Participant in
writing, including the Participant’ s current mailing address, age and marital status. The Plan Administrator ’s
interpretations, determinations, regulations and calculations shall be final and binding on all persons and parties
concerned. Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator shall be a fiduciary of the Plan, and any restrictions that
might apply to a party in interest under section 406 of ERISA shall not apply under the Plan, including with respect to
the Company or the Plan Administrator .
7.2    Facility of Payment : Whenever , in the Plan Administrator ’s opinion, a person entitled to receive
any payment of a benefit or installment thereof hereunder is under a legal disability or is incapacitated in any way so
as to be unable to manage his financial af fairs, the Plan Administrator may make payments to such person or to the
legal representative of such person for his benefit, or the Plan Administrator may apply the payment for the benefit of
such person in such manner as it considers advisable. Any payment of a benefit or installment thereof in accordance
with the provisions of this section shall be a complete discharge of any liability for the making of such payment under
the provisions of the Plan.
7.3    Claims Procedure : The Plan Administrator , or a party designated by the Plan Administrator , shall
have the exclusive discretionary authority to construe and to interpret
- 73 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthe Plan, to decide all questions of eligibility for benefits and to determine the amount of such benefits. As a result,
benefits under this Plan will be paid only if the Plan Administrator decides in its discretion that the Participant (or other
applicant) is entitled to them. Any decisions or determinations hereunder shall be made in the absolute and
unrestricted discretion of the Plan Administrator , even if (i) such discretion is not expressly granted by the Plan
provisions in question, or (ii) a decision or determination is not expressly called for by the Plan provisions in question,
and even though other Plan provisions expressly grant discretion or expressly call for a decision or determination. All
decisions and determinations made by the Plan Administrator will be final, conclusive, and binding on all parties. The
Plan Administrator may consider the intent of the Company with respect to a Plan provision in making any
determination with respect to the provision, notwithstanding the provisions set forth in any document that arguably do
not contemplate considering such intent. The Plan Administrator ’s discretion is absolute, and in any case where the
breadth of the Plan Administrator ’s discretion is at issue, it is expressly intended that the Plan Administrator (or its
delegate) be accorded the maximum possible discretion. Any exercise by the Plan Administrator of its discretionary
authority shall be reviewed by a court under the arbitrary and capricious standard (i.e., abuse of discretion). If,
pursuant to this discretionary authority , an assertion of any right to a benefit by or on behalf of a Participant or
beneficiary (a “claimant”) is wholly or partially denied, the Plan Administrator , or a party designated by the Plan
Administrator , will provide such claimant within the 90-day period following the receipt of the claim by the Plan
Administrator , a comprehensible written notice setting forth:
(a)    The specific reason or reasons for such denial;
- 74 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(b)    Specific reference to pertinent Plan provisions on which the denial is based;
(c)    A description of any additional material or information necessary for the claimant to submit
to perfect the claim and an explanation of why such material or information is necessary; and
(d)    A description of the Plan’ s claim review procedure (including the time limits applicable to
such process and a statement of the claimant’ s right to bring a civil action under ERISA following a further
denial on review).
If the Plan Administrator determines that special circumstances require an extension of time for processing the claim
it may extend the response period from 90 to 180 days. If this occurs, the Plan Administrator will notify the claimant
before the end of the initial 90-day period, indicating the special circumstances requiring the extension and the date
by which the Plan Committee expects to make the final decision. The claim review procedure is available upon
written request by the claimant to the Plan Administrator , or the designated party , within 60 days after receipt by the
claimant of written notice of the denial of the claim. Upon review , the Plan Administrator shall provide the claimant a
full and fair review of the claim, including the opportunity to submit to the Plan Administrator comments, document,
records and other information relevant to the claim and the Plan Administrator ’s review shall take into account such
comments, documents, records and information regardless of whether it was submitted or considered at the initial
determination. The decision on review will be made within 60 days after receipt of the request for review , unless
circumstances warrant an extension of time not to exceed an additional 60 days. If this occurs, notice of the extension
will be furnished to the claimant before the end of the initial 60-day period, indicating the special circumstances
- 75 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programrequiring the extension and the date by which the Plan Administrator expects to make the final decision. The final
decision shall be in writing and drafted in a manner calculated to be understood by the claimant; include specific
reasons for the decision with references to the specific Plan provisions on which the decision is based; and provide
that the claimant is entitled to receive, upon request ad free of charge, reasonable access to, and copies of, all
documents, records, and other information relevant to his or her claim for benefits.
Any claim under the Plan that is reviewed by a court, arbitrator or any other tribunal shall be reviewed
solely on the basis of the record before the Plan Administrator at the time it made its determination. In addition, any
such review shall be conditioned on the claimant’ s having fully exhausted all rights under this section as is more fully
explained in Section 7.5. Any notice or other notification that is required to be sent to a claimant under this section
may be sent pursuant to any method approved under Department of Labor Regulation Section 2520.104b-1 or other
applicable guidance.
7.4    Effect of Specific References : Specific references in the Plan to the Plan Administrator ’s discretion
shall create no inference that the Plan Administrator ’s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other
provision, is less complete or broad.
7.5    Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’ s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court:  Before filing any
Claim (including a suit or other action) in court or in another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully exhaust all of the
Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedures of Section 7.3.
(a)    Upon review by any court or other tribunal, the exhaustion requirement of this Section 7.5 is
intended to be interpreted to require exhaustion in as

(b)    In any action or consideration of a Claim in court or in another tribunal following exhaustion

(d)    The Plan Administrator may make special arrangements to consider a Claim on a class
basis or to address unusual conflicts concerns, and such minimum arrangements in these respects shall be

(e)     For example, exhaustion may not be excused (i) for failure to respond to a claim unless the
purported Claimant took steps that were suf ficient to make it reasonably clear to the Plan Administrator that
the purported Claimant was

(f)    For purposes of this Section 7.5, the following definitions apply .

title: Miscellaneous
heading:
ARTICLE VIII
Miscellaneous
start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of an Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to discharge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
summary:
- Employment not guaranteed: The Plan does not create a contract of employment or restrict an employer’s right to terminate employment with or without cause.
- Anti‑alienation of benefits: Plan benefits cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, garnished, or otherwise encumbered, including in divorce or child-support matters; the Company is not liable for beneficiaries’ debts.
- Unfunded status: Obligations are paid from the Company’s general assets; participants are unsecured general creditors.
- Corporate authority: Plan actions may be taken by the Board, its Compensation Committee, or duly authorized designees, with reporting to the Board.
- Indemnification: Employees administering the Plan in good faith are indemnified to the fullest extent permitted by law unless the Board decides otherwise.
- Section 409A compliance: The Plan is intended to comply with 409A; good‑faith actions to comply do not create liability. Explicit anti‑duplication rules ensure no double counting of benefit elements (e.g., earnings or service), with specific provisions controlling over general ones and integration rules with the Salaried Plan.
- Section 457A measures for expatriates: For Covered Transfers to certain non‑U.S. entities, participants vest immediately before transfer (unless the Company issues a contrary communication); post‑transfer benefit enhancements tied to service or age are credited only at plan year‑end and only if permissible; no right to enhancements that would be taxable under 457A; these rules cease upon return to qualifying U.S. entities or as specified by Company communication.
- Authorized transfers outside PepsiCo: If a participant moves to a non‑PepsiCo entity, liability for accrued benefits remains with the Company unless otherwise agreed.
- Electronic signatures: Electronic signatures and records are fully valid and enforceable to the extent permitted by law.
- Amendment and termination (Article IX overview): The Company retains broad rights, subject to 409A, to amend (including retroactively) or terminate the Plan at any time; continuation is not guaranteed. Amendments/termination cannot reduce the benefit amount already earned under Article IV as of the action date unless an equal amount is provided under another plan or as necessary to comply with 409A; specific payment forms are not protected. Only the Company may amend. The termination provision begins to outline options to terminate the Plan as to the Company or specific employers/groups.

title: Amendment and Termination
heading:
ARTICLE IX
Amendment and T ermination
start_phrase: This Article governs the Company’ s right to amend and or terminate the Plan.
summary:
- Article IX outlines the Company’s authority to amend or terminate the Plan, subject at all times to Internal Revenue Code Section 409A. The Company’s powers are as broad as allowed by law.
- Continuation: Although intended to continue indefinitely, the Plan may be amended, terminated, or partially terminated at the Company’s discretion. Amendments or terminations cannot reduce a participant’s accrued benefit under Article IV as of the action date unless an equal benefit is provided under another plan or as necessary to comply with Section 409A. Specific payment forms are not protected.
- Amendments: The Company alone may amend the Plan, including retroactively, to ensure continued 409A compliance. Other Employers have no amendment rights.
- Termination: The Company may terminate the Plan in whole or for specific Employers, for a group experiencing a change in control under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), or as otherwise permitted by Section 409A. If not all Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for remaining Employers. Distributions upon termination must follow 409A restrictions.
- Change in Control: The Company retains maximum discretionary authority permitted by 409A to terminate and make distributions in connection with a Change in Control (as defined in 409A). These are the exclusive terms for any Change in Control distribution of 409A Program-derived benefits.
- Article X (ERISA Plan Structure): Together with the Pre-409A Program documents, the Plan consists of three separate ERISA plans (effective July 1, 1996):
  - Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): Provides benefits above Internal Revenue Code §415 limits for Salaried Plan participants.
  - Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing benefits above Code §401(a)(17) limits (after accounting for the Excess Benefit Plan); for ERISA reporting, referred to as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
  - Preservation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees that preserves certain benefits for Salaried Plan participants (description truncated in the excerpt).

title: ERISA Plan Structure
heading:
ARTICLE X
ERISA Plan Structure
start_phrase: This Plan document in conjunction with the plan document(s) for the Pre-409A Program encompasses three separate plans within the meaning of ERISA, as are set forth in subsections (a), (b) and (c).
summary:
- Establishes the ERISA plan structure for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program), which, together with Pre-409A plan documents, comprises three separate ERISA plans effective July 1, 1996 (with plans (b) and (c) previously a single plan).
- Defines three components:
  - Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): provides benefits exceeding Internal Revenue Code §415 limits for Salaried Plan participants.
  - Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: a “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing benefits above the §401(a)(17) compensation cap under the Salaried Plan (after the Excess Benefit Plan); ERISA reporting name: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
  - Preservation Top Hat Plan: a “top hat” plan preserving pre-1989 accrual levels for certain participants described in §5.2(a), after taking into account the other two plans; ERISA reporting name: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan II.
- Specifies benefit allocation order: first to the Excess Benefit Plan; then to the Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan; then to the Preservation Top Hat Plan. Confirms the three plans are severable for all purposes.
- Clarifies that lump-sum termination benefits paid in connection with Special Early Retirement under a temporary company severance program are treated as part of an unfunded severance (welfare) plan under ERISA §3(1), exist only for the program’s duration and purpose, and are not subject to top hat reporting or pension-plan ERISA requirements.
- Sets governing law: ERISA and applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; New York law applies where not preempted by ERISA.
- Includes a severability clause: invalidity of any provision does not affect the remainder of the Plan.
text:
ARTICLE X
ERISA Plan Structure
This Plan document in conjunction with the plan document(s) for the Pre-409A Program encompasses
three separate plans within the meaning of ERISA, as are set forth in subsections (a), (b) and (c). This division into
separate plans became ef fective as of July 1, 1996; previously the plans set forth in subsections (b) and (c) were a
single plan within the meaning of ERISA.
(a)    Excess Benefit Plan : An excess benefit plan within the meaning of section 3(36) of ERISA,
maintained solely for the purpose of providing benefits for Salaried Plan participants in excess of the limitations
on benefits imposed by section 415 of the Code.
(b)    Excess Compensation T op Hat Plan : A plan maintained by the Company primarily for the
purpose of providing deferred compensation for a select group of management or highly compensated
employees within the meaning of sections 201(2) and 401(a)(1) of ERISA. The plan provides benefits for
Salaried Plan participants in excess of the limitations imposed by section 401(a)(17) of the Code on benefits
under the Salaried Plan (after taking into account any benefits under the Excess Benefit Plan). For ERISA
reporting purposes, this portion of PEP may be referred to as the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
(c)    Preservation T op Hat Plan : A plan maintained by the Company primarily for the purpose of
providing deferred compensation for a select group of management or highly compensated employees within
the meaning of sections 201(2) and 401(a)(1) of ERISA. The plan provides preserves benefits for those
Salaried Plan
- 89 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programparticipants described in section 5.2(a) hereof, by preserving for them the pre-1989 level of benefit accrual that
was in ef fect before the Salaried Plan’ s amendment ef fective January 1, 1989 (after taking into account any
benefits under the Excess Benefit Plan and Excess Compensation T op Hat Plan). For ERISA reporting
purposes, this portion of PEP shall be referred to as the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan II.
Benefits under this Plan shall be allocated first to the Excess Benefit Plan, to the extent of benefits paid for the
purpose indicated in (a) above; then any remaining benefits shall be allocated to the Excess Compensation T op Hat
Plan, to the extent of benefits paid for the purpose indicated in (b) above; then any remaining benefits shall be
allocated to the Preservation T op Hat Plan. These three plans are severable for any and all purposes as directed by
the Company .
In addition to the above, to the extent that lump sum termination benefits are paid under this Plan in
connection with a severed employee’ s Special Early Retirement (as defined in Appendix Article D) under a temporary
severance program sponsored by the Company , this portion of the Plan shall be a component of the Company’ s
unfunded severance plan that includes the temporary program of severance benefits in question. As a component of
a severance plan, the lump sum termination benefits are welfare benefits, and this portion is part of a “welfare benefit
plan” under ERISA section 3(1). This severance plan component shall exist solely (i) for the duration of the temporary
severance program in question, and (ii) for the purpose of paying severance benefits. As a portion of an ERISA
welfare plan, any such temporary severance benefits hereunder shall not be subject to the reporting requirements for
top hat plans under ERISA or any of the ERISA requirements for pension plans.

PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program

title: Transition Provisions
heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE A - 
Transition Provisions
start_phrase: This Article A provides the transition rules for the Plan that were ef fective at some time during the period beginning January 1, 2005 and ending December 31, 2008 (the “T ransition Period”).
summary:
- Scope and timing: Establishes transition rules for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program effective during January 1, 2005–December 31, 2008, specifying when each provision applied.

- Definitions adjustments (Article II):
  - Actuarial Equivalent: During the transition, annuity conversions for certain forms (QJSA, survivor annuities with inflation protection, Single Life Annuity) used Salaried Plan actuarial factors.
  - Key Employee identification: Special interim rules for 2005–2007, broadly treating Band IV+ (and grandfathered equivalents) as Key Employees and setting compensation-based lookbacks (under Code §415(c)(3)) by calendar quarter to determine Key status.

- Distributions (Article VI): 409A Pensions that otherwise would have been paid during the transition were instead paid on March 1, 2009.

- Administration (Article VII): Replaced Section 8.6(a) to mandate compliance with Code §409A and preservation of grandfathered (Pre-409A) deferrals; voids actions/provisions that would violate §409A or harm grandfathering; deems required §409A provisions included.

- Severance benefits transition rules:
  - Defines Special Early Retirement (age 50–<55 with 10 years of Elapsed Time Service; for 2008 severance, age/service rounded up).
  - 2005 severance: Sets payment timing/form for non-retirement-eligible (paid as Vested Pension; coordination with Salaried Plan timing; special 2007 payment timing for some) and for retirement-eligible or Special Early Retirement participants (generally lump sum first of month after separation).
  - 2007 severance: Distinguishes non-retirement-eligible (Vested Pension forms), retirement-eligible (lump sum unless valid prior payment election), those becoming retirement-eligible during paid leave, Special Early Retirement eligible or becoming eligible during leave; specifies “PEP Kicker” lump sum timing and interaction with prior payment elections.
  - 2008 severance: Parallel structure to 2007 with timing/forms, inclusion of Special Early Retirement rules (with rounding), and PEP Kicker handling.
  - Key Employee delay: If a payment is due on account of Separation from Service and the participant is a Key Employee, applies the payment delay under Section 6.6.
  - Compliance: Confirms company elections and payments complied with Notice 2005-1 and Code §409A (including 19(c)) and were scheduled in the termination year as specified.

- Special participant rules:
  - For 2005 Band VI limited-duration assignments (<5 years): Deems 5 years of PEP Credited Service and vesting.
  - For a participant with a 11/1/2007 Salaried Plan lump-sum Annuity Starting Date (selected 10/9/2007): Non-409A portion of Plan benefit paid as a lump sum six months after that date.
  - For a participant who fixed a 2/1/2005 payment date (selected 9/3/2004): Confirms that as the commencement date and includes service during post-payment consulting in benefit calculation.

- 409A Disability Pension (Pre-Separation Accruals):
  - Distributions start March 1, 2009, using Vested Pension forms (married/unmarried differences apply).
  - Additional death benefit: If death occurs before expected mortality date, beneficiary receives a lump sum actuarial equivalent of remaining expected payments; sets beneficiary designation hierarchy.

- Appendix B (Severance window earnings/service computation):
  - Defines Severance Program and Eligible Bonus.
  - Allows salary continuation and Eligible Bonus earned in the first 12 months of a qualifying severance leave to be included in Highest Average Monthly Earnings, even if paid later, with references to recognizing Service and Credited Service under Sections B.3 and B.4.

heading:
