Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance W indows
start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases, in boldface and underlined, appear in this Appendix B with initial capitals they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
summary:
- The excerpt is from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program and covers Appendix Article B (Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance Windows) and the start of Appendix Article C (International and PIRP Transfer Participants).

- Article B defines key terms:
  - Severance Program: A severance benefit program that the Plan Administrator deems eligible for recognizing Service and Credited Service under this appendix.
  - Eligible Bonus: An annual incentive under the Severance Program that can be included in Highest Average Monthly Earnings.

- Article B outlines how severance-related pay and time can be credited:
  - Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus (B.2): Salary continuation and Eligible Bonus for the first 12 months of a severance leave can be counted toward Highest Average Monthly Earnings, even if paid after Separation from Service; projected amounts may be used if pension benefits commence before all payments are made.
  - Inclusion of Credited Service (B.3): The first 12 months of severance can count as Credited Service for calculating the Participant’s Pension and pre-retirement spouse/eligible domestic partner benefits, even if this period is after Separation from Service.
  - Inclusion of Service (B.4): Similarly, the first 12 months of severance can count as Service for these benefits, even if after Separation from Service.
  - Reduction to Reflect Early Payment (B.5): If pension calculations include projected service or earnings before they are actually performed or paid, the benefit is actuarially adjusted using the Salaried Plan’s early payment rate to account for the early inclusion.

- Article C introduces special calculation rules for certain transfers:
  - Scope (C.1): Establishes special benefit rules for International Transfer Participants and PIRP Transfer Participants; benefits are paid under normal plan terms and are subject to Code section 409A (including amounts accrued before 1/1/2005). Effective dates: International Transfer rules effective 4/1/2007; PIRP Transfer rules effective 1/1/2016 (with possible pre-2016 service recognition).
  - International Transfer Participants (C.2): Begins defining who qualifies, referencing transfers to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary” and specific employee status criteria under the Salaried Plan; full definition continues beyond the excerpt.

APPENDIX ARTICLE B - 
Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance W indows     
B.1    Definitions :
Where the following words and phrases, in boldface and underlined, appear in this Appendix B with initial
capitals they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context. Any
terms used in this Article B of the Appendix with initial capitals and not defined herein shall have the same meaning
as in the main Plan, unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
(a)    “ Severance Program ” shall mean a program providing certain severance benefits that are paid
while the program’ s participants are on a severance leave of absence that is determined by the Plan
Administrator to qualify for recognition as Service under Section B.3 and Credited Service under Section B.4 of
Article B.
(b)    “ Eligible Bonus ” shall mean an annual incentive payment that is payable to the Participant under
the Severance Program and that is identified under the terms of the Severance Program as eligible for
inclusion in determining the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings.
B.2    Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus :
The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window
program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit pursuant to a Severance Program,
all salary continuation and any Eligible Bonus earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of a leave of absence
period provided to the Participant under such Severance Program will be counted toward the Participant’ s Highest
Average Monthly Earnings, even if such salary or other earnings are to be received after a
- 109 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramParticipant’ s Separation from Service. In particular , if payment of a Participant’ s 409A Pension is to be made at
Separation from Service and prior to the Participant’ s receipt of all of the salary continuation or Eligible Bonus that is
payable to the Participant from the Severance Program, the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings shall be
determined by taking into account the full salary continuation and eligible bonus that is projected to be payable to the
Participant during the first 12 months of a period of leave of absence that is granted to the Participant under the
Severance Program.
B.3    Inclusion of Credited Service :
The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window
program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit under a Severance Program, all
Credited Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of the period of severance will be counted toward
the Participant’ s Credited Service for purposes of determining the Participant’ s Pension and a Pre-Retirement
Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Eligible Domestic Partner ’s Pension, even if the period of time counted as
Credited Service under the Severance Program occurs after a Participant’ s Separation from Service.
B.4    Inclusion of Service :
The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window
program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit under a Severance Program, all
Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of the period of severance will be counted toward the
Participant’ s Service for purposes of determining the Participant’ s Pension and a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension
or Pre-
- 110 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramRetirement Eligible Domestic Partner ’s Pension, even if the period of time counted as Service under the Severance
Program occurs after a Participant’ s Separation from Service.
B.5    Reduction to Reflect Early Payment :
If the Participant receives either (1) additional Credited Service or (2) additional earnings that are included in
Highest A verage Monthly Earnings under Sections B.2 or B.3 of this Article B, as a result of a severance benefit
provided under a Severance Program and such additional Credited Service or earnings are included in the calculation
of the Participant’ s Pension prior to the time that the Credited Service is actually performed by the Participant, or the
earnings are actually paid to the Participant, the Pension paid to the Participant shall be adjusted actuarially to reflect
the receipt of the portion of the Pension attributable to such Credited Service or earnings received on account of the
Severance Program prior to the time such Credited Service is performed or such earnings are actually paid to the
Participant. For purposes of determining the adjustment to be made, the Plan shall use the rate provided under the
Salaried Plan for early payment of benefits.

International and PIRP T ransfer Participants
start_phrase: This Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of an individual who is either an “International Transfer Participant” under Section C.2 below or a “PIRP T ransfer Participant” under Section C.4 below .
summary: This article sets special rules for calculating benefits for International Transfer Participants (defined in C.2) and PIRP Transfer Participants (definitions introduced in C.4), with benefits determined under C.3/C.5 respectively, then paid under the Plan’s normal terms and subject to Code section 409A (including pre‑2005 accruals); provisions are effective April 1, 2007 for International Transfers and January 1, 2016 for PIRP (which may consider earlier years). An International Transfer Participant is one transferred to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary” who would meet the Salaried Plan Part B Section 2.1 Employee definition paragraph (2)(vi) (U.S. citizen or resident alien on qualifying temporary international assignment) but for holding a Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher role, including a special Mexico rule requiring Band 4+, Mexico listed as home country with the Expat Centre for Excellence (or successor), and an assignment not limited to 5 years; pre‑April 1, 2007 transfers qualify if these conditions were met at transfer. For transfers that occurred before 1992, service and earnings with the foreign subsidiary prior to 1992 are excluded.

- Overall intent: Coordinate and equalize pension benefits for employees transferring between U.S. and international plans, ensure recognition of service and compensation despite accrual blocks, and avoid benefit duplication through specified offsets.

summary:

start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix E with initial capitals, they shall have the meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
summary:
The excerpt outlines Appendix Article E of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, governing when and how benefits are paid during severance windows.

Key points:
- Scope and effective dates: Applies to participants terminated under a Severance Program or qualifying Individual Severance Agreement on/after Jan 1, 2009 (or Jan 1, 2012 for those under Appendix Article PBG). Clarifies that severance-related enhancements are not permanent plan features.
- Defined terms:
  - Applicable Summary Plan Description: Governs a specific Severance Program.
  - Covered Participant: A participant whose employment ends and who qualifies for Special Early Retirement via a Severance Program or Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Individual Severance Agreement: An agreement that sets termination terms and explicitly qualifies the participant for Special Early Retirement under PEP.
  - Kicker: The Special Early Retirement benefit equal to the difference between the Early Retirement Pension and the Vested Pension across the Salaried Plan and this Plan, split into:
    - PEP Kicker (nonqualified plan replacement benefits), and
    - Qualified Kicker (qualified plan replacement benefits).
    Early retirement reduction factors before age 55 generally use the 56-to-55 rate unless a Severance Program or Individual Severance Agreement specifies otherwise.
  - Severance Program: As defined in the Salaried Plan (cross-referenced).
  - Special Early Retirement: Meets SPD conditions or is expressly recognized in an Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Termination Date: The later of Separation from Service or the projected end of any severance leave; fixed based on formulas in effect when the right to special early retirement arises and does not change due to later events.
- Payment timing/form for 409A Pension (excluding the Kicker):
  - If not retirement-eligible at Separation: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with forms under Section 6.2.
  - If retirement-eligible (Normal, Early, or Late) at Separation: paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), or per a valid prior election under Section 6.1(a)(2).

(e)    “ Severance Program ” has the same meaning that applies to that term under Appendix Section
ERW.2(f) of Part B of the Salaried Plan (legacy PepsiCo Appendix).
(f)    “ Special Early Retirement ” means a retirement from the Company that either – (i) satisfies all of the
conditions for receiving special early retirement benefits that are set forth in an Applicable Summary Plan
Description, or (ii) is expressly recognized as qualifying for special early retirement benefits pursuant to the
terms of an Individual Severance Agreement.
(g)    “ Termination Date ” means the later of – (i) the Covered Participant’ s Separation from Service, or
(ii) date as of which the Covered Participant’ s severance leave of absence (if any) is projected to terminate
under the terms of the Applicable Summary Plan Description or the Individual Severance Agreement, as
applicable. If clause (ii) of the preceding sentence applies, then a Participant’ s Termination Date shall

PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programbe determined as of the date of the Participant’ s Separation from Service using the formulas for calculating the
severance leave of absence, as such formulas are in ef fect under the Applicable Summary Plan Description or
the Individual Severance Agreement when the legally binding right to special early retirement benefits arises in
connection with the Severance Program or pursuant to the Individual Severance Agreement. A Participant’ s

title: Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension
heading: E.3 Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension :
start_phrase: A Covered Participant’ s 409A Pension (calculated without regard to the Kicker for purposes of this Section E.3) shall be paid as follows:
summary:
- Establishes how a Participant’s Termination Date is determined at Separation from Service, using severance leave-of-absence formulas in the applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement when special early retirement rights arise; once set, the Termination Date does not change due to later events.
- Defines time and form of payment for the 409A Pension (excluding any Kicker in the calculation for this section):
  - Non-retirement eligible at Separation: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with form options under Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible (Normal, Early, or Late) at Separation: paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), or per a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2).
  - Becomes Normal/Early retirement eligible after Separation (including during paid leave): paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with form options under Section 6.2.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at Separation or becomes eligible during paid leave: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with form options under Section 6.2.
- Specifies time and form of Kicker benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s 55th birthday or Separation from Service; a valid prior election under Section 6.1(a)(2) governs even if the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under E.3(b)(2). If the Participant dies after qualifying but before payment, the PEP Kicker is paid in a lump sum to the Surviving Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.
- Applies to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, referencing Sections 6.1(a)(1), 6.1(a)(2), 6.1(b), 6.2, and Article IV.
text:
E.3    Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension :
A Covered Participant’ s 409A Pension (calculated without regard to the Kicker for purposes of this Section
E.3) shall be paid as follows:

Article IV as of his Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a
Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1); provided, however , that if the Participant made a valid prior
payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2), his 409A Pension shall be paid as a Retirement Pension in
accordance with such election.

PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(2)    If the Covered Participant becomes eligible for a Normal or Early Retirement Pension after
his Separation from Service, including during the period between his Separation from Service and the
last day of his paid leave of absence (if any), the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a V ested
Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to V ested

title: Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits
heading: E.4 Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits :
start_phrase: A Covered Participant’ s PEP Kicker and Qualified Kicker shall be paid as follows:
summary:
- Defines how a 409A Pension is paid if a participant becomes eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement after Separation from Service (including during any paid leave period): it is treated and paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) following the form-of-payment rules in Section 6.2.
- Specifies timing and form of payment for “kicker” benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) controls even if the 409A Pension is paid differently. If the participant dies after qualifying but before payment, it is paid in a lump sum within 60 days to the Surviving Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or otherwise to the estate.
  - Qualified Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the Termination Date, unless an Applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement specifies a different time or form; death benefits follow the same 60-day spouse/partner-then-estate rule.
- Establishes a payment delay requirement for Key Employees: any payment triggered by Separation from Service is delayed per Section 6.6, unless an exemption from Section 409A applies.
text:

title: Delay for Key Employees
heading: E.5 Delay for Key Employees :
start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provision of this Appendix E to the contrary , if a Participant is determined to be a Key Employee, any payment under this Article E that is made on account of his Separation from Service shall be subject to the required delay in payment for Key Employees under Section 6.6, except to the extent that the payment qualifies for an exemption from the application of Section 409A.
summary:
- Sets payment rules for a “Qualified Kicker” benefit: generally paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the participant’s termination date, unless an Applicable Summary Plan Description (SPD) or Individual Severance Agreement specifies a different time or form, in which case that document governs.
- Establishes death payment provisions: if a participant qualifies for a benefit (including the Qualified Kicker) but dies before payment, the benefit is paid in a single lump sum 60 days after death to the surviving spouse or eligible domestic partner, or to the estate if none.
- Imposes a Section 409A “Key Employee” delay: if the participant is a Key Employee, any payment triggered by separation from service under Article E is delayed in accordance with Section 6.6, except where a 409A exemption applies.
- Introduces Appendix F (U.K. Supplementary Appendix for Participants with U.S. Service):
  - Scope: applies to “Covered U.K. Employees”; benefits are determined under Section F.3, paid under the plan’s normal time and form rules, and are subject to Code section 409A; Appendix restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011 for pre-2016 service).
  - Defines “Covered U.K. Employee” criteria: a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who (i) becomes subject to U.S. income taxes by engaging in U.S. service, (ii) continues accruing benefits under the U.K. plan during U.S. service, (iii) would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix but for its unavailability during U.S. service, (iv) later is either localized in the U.S. or terminates employment before starting an assignment outside the U.S., and (v) after satisfying those conditions, is designated as covered (designation details continue beyond the excerpt).

F.1    Scope:
This Article applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F .2 below . The benefit of a Covered
U.K. Employee shall be determined as provided in Section F .3 below . Once a benefit is determined for a Covered
U.K. Employee under this Article, it shall be paid in accordance with the Plan’ s normal terms regarding the time and
form of payment. All benefits payable under this Article are subject to Code section 409A. This Article has been

title: “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined
heading: F.2 “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined :
start_phrase: A “Covered U.K. Employee” is a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan (“U.K. Participant”) who – (i) becomes subject to United States income taxes, e.g., by transferring to a position with the Company in the United States or otherwise
summary:
- Establishes Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for U.K. employees who perform U.S. service, restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011), with all benefits subject to Code section 409A and paid under the Plan’s standard timing and form rules.
- Defines “Covered U.K. Employee” as a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who: (i) becomes subject to U.S. income taxes (Engages in U.S. Service); (ii) continues accruing under the U.K. Pension Plan during U.S. Service; (iii) would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix for that period but for its unavailability during U.S. Service; (iv) is later either localized in the U.S. or terminates employment before starting a non-U.S. assignment; and (v) after meeting all prior conditions, is designated by the Company in its sole discretion, creating a binding right to Article F benefits. The U.S. Service period runs from the U.S. Commencement Date (first subject to U.S. tax) to the U.S. Cessation Date (no longer subject to U.S. tax or earlier if Article F benefits commence).
- Describes benefit determination for Covered U.K. Employees as the Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit minus the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit, measured as of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date.
  - Modified U.S. Cessation Date is the earliest of: ceasing U.S. tax status; first satisfying localization/termination condition; starting an assignment outside the U.S.; or Article F benefit commencement.
  - Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit equals the benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix based on all service and compensation through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date that is (or would be but for U.K. legal limits) counted under the U.K. Pension Plan, expressed as a single lump sum payable when Article F benefits commence.
- Notes that the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is subtracted in the formula, though its definition appears beyond the provided excerpt.
text:
F.2    “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined :
A “Covered U.K. Employee” is a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan (“U.K. Participant”) who – (i)
becomes subject to United States income taxes, e.g., by transferring to a position with the Company in the United
States or otherwise (hereinafter referenced as “Engages in U.S. Service”), (ii) continues to accrue benefits under the
PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after he Engages in U.S. Service, (iii) would have also accrued a benefit under the U.K.
Supplementary Pension Appendix for such period following when he Engages in U.S. Service (except for the
unavailability of accruals under such Appendix for the period a U.K. Participant Engages in U.S. Service), (iv)
subsequently either – (A) is localized in the United States as an employee of the PepsiCo Organization, or (B)
terminates employment with the PepsiCo Organization (provided this occurs before the date the U.K. Participant
commences an assignment with the PepsiCo Organization that is located outside the United States, as defined in the
Code), and (v) only after fully satisfying all of the preceding clauses, is then designated by
- 127 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthe Company (in its completely unfettered discretion) as a Covered U.K. Employee and thereby granted a legally
binding right to a benefit under this Article F at the time of the designation. The period that a U.K. Participant Engages
in U.S. Service shall begin on the first day that he becomes subject to United States income taxes (his “U.S.
Commencement Date”), and it shall end on the date he is no longer subject to U.S. income taxes or , if earlier , the
date his Plan benefits under this Article F commence (his “U.S. Cessation Date”).

title: Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees
heading: F.3 Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees :
start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating, as of his Modified U.S. Cessation Date, his “T otal U.K. Supplementary Benefit” and then subtracting from this amount his “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit.”
summary:
- Establishes that the Company, in its sole discretion, may designate certain individuals as Covered U.K. Employees, which grants a legally binding right to an Article F benefit.
- Defines U.S. Service timing based on U.S. income tax status:
  - U.S. Commencement Date: first day the employee becomes subject to U.S. income taxes.
  - U.S. Cessation Date: when the employee is no longer subject to U.S. income taxes or, if earlier, when Article F benefits commence.
- Sets the Article F benefit formula for Covered U.K. Employees as:
  - Benefit = Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit (as of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date) minus Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit (as of immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date), with both expressed as a single lump sum payable when Article F benefits commence.
- Defines key terms:
  - Modified U.S. Cessation Date: earliest of (i) no longer subject to U.S. income taxes, (ii) first satisfying clause (iv) of Section F.2, (iii) starting an assignment outside the United States, or (iv) Article F benefit commencement.
  - Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit: the total benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix, based on all service and compensation through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date that is (or would be but for U.K. legal limits) counted under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan, expressed as a lump sum payable at Article F commencement.
  - Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit: the benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, expressed as a lump sum payable at Article F commencement.
- Provides operating rules for calculations:
  - Accruals under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after the U.S. Cessation Date generally do not reduce the Article F benefit.
  - If those post-cessation accruals more than fully offset accruals under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix, the excess may offset Article F benefits, but only to the extent permitted under Code Section 409A.
  - Lump-sum valuations must use actuarial assumptions that comply with applicable Code/Section 409A requirements.

F.3    Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees :
A Covered U.K. Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating, as of his Modified U.S.

assignment with the PepsiCo Organization that is located outside the United States (as defined in the Code),

PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan (or that would be counted but for a limitation applicable to the plan under U.K.
law), and with such total benefit expressed in the form of a single lump sum that is payable as of the date his
benefits under this Article F commence, and

title: Operating Rules
heading: F.4 Operating Rules:
start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation in Section F .3. above.
summary:
- Defines “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit” as the lump-sum value, determined at Article F commencement, of the participant’s accrued benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix as of immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, calculated per Section F.4.
- Operating rules for calculating the Article F benefit:
  - Post–U.S. Cessation Date accruals in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan generally do not reduce the Article F benefit; however, any excess accruals that would have offset Supplementary Appendix benefits may offset the Article F benefit to the extent permitted by Code Section 409A.
  - Lump-sum valuations must use Code Section 417(e) actuarial assumptions as applied under the Salaried Plan at the relevant determination date.
  - The Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is determined assuming the participant voluntarily terminated immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date.
  - If mid‑year amendments to the U.K. Plan or Supplementary Appendix would alter the Section F.3 result, application is delayed to the following year as necessary to comply with Code Section 409A.
  - If the participant later re-enters U.S. Service and again qualifies as a Covered U.K. Employee, Article F applies anew; any new benefit is reduced by the lump-sum value of prior Article F benefits to avoid duplication.
  - If the participant later becomes eligible for benefits under other provisions of the Plan, any such benefit is reduced by the lump-sum value of prior Article F benefits to avoid duplication.
- No other benefits are payable under this Plan or the Salaried Plan while the individual is (or would be but for specified clauses) a Covered U.K. Employee.
- Before an individual satisfies all requirements to be a Covered U.K. Employee, there is no legally binding right to an Article F benefit; the Company retains unfettered discretion to deny designation and prevent entitlement, regardless of services performed, until all requirements are met.
text:
F.4    Operating Rules:
The following operating rules apply to the calculation in Section F .3. above.
(a)    In general, accruals under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan for the period after a Covered U.K.
Employee’ s U.S. Cessation Date shall not reduce the benefit under this Article F determined under Section
F.3. Notwithstanding the prior sentence and anything in Section F .3 to the contrary , to the extent a Covered
U.K. Employee’ s accruals under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan for the period after a Covered U.K.
Employee’ s U.S. Cessation Date have more than fully of fset the Covered U.K. Employee’ s accruals under the
U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix (and the excess would have been of fset against the benefit under this
Article F had such benefit accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Appendix), then any such excess as of the
date benefits under this Article F commence (expressed as a lump sum as of such date) shall be of fset against
the benefits under this Article F to the extent such of fset would not violate Code Section 409A.
(b)    In determining the value of a lump sum under this Article F , the actuarial assumptions that are
used shall be actuarial assumptions that comply with Section
- 129 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program417(e) of the Code and, specifically , are the Code Section 417(e) assumptions that would be used under the
Salaried Plan to pay a retirement lump sum as of the date applicable that the lump sum in question is to be
determined under this Article F .
(c)    A Covered U.K. Employee’ s Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit shall be determined on the basis
of assuming that the Covered U.K. employee voluntarily terminated employment and any other service
relationship with the PepsiCo Organization as of immediately before his U.S. Commencement Date.
(d)    This subsection applies if the terms of the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan or the U.K. Supplementary
Pension Appendix are amended during a year in a way that would change the results under the Section F .3
calculation, and such amendment otherwise applies earlier than the immediately following year . In this case, to
the extent that doing is necessary to comply with Code Section 409A, the calculation in Section F .3 shall be
made by delaying the application of the amendment so that it is prospectively ef fective starting with the
immediately following year .
(e)    In the event a Covered U.K. Employee (i) has earned a benefit under this Article F , (ii) has reached
his U.S. Cessation Date, and (iii) then again Engages in U.S. Service and meets all of the requirements to be a
Covered U.K. Employee when he again Engages in U.S. Service, the foregoing terms shall be applied again to
determine if he earns a benefit for the new period that he Engages in U.S. Service, except that any resulting
benefit from this new period shall be reduced by the lump sum value of any prior benefit under this Article F
(as necessary to completely avoid any duplication of benefits).
- 130 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(f)    In the event a Covered U.K. Employee (i) has earned a benefit under this Article F , (ii) has reached
his U.S. Cessation Date, and (iii) then is employed by the PepsiCo Organization in a classification that would
be eligible for an accrual under the provisions of the Plan other than this Article F (the “Other Provisions”), then
the Other Provisions shall be applied to determine if he earns a benefit under the Other Provisions for the new
period of service, except that any resulting benefit from this new period of service shall be reduced by the lump
sum value of any prior benefit under this Article F (as necessary to completely avoid any duplication of
benefits).

title: No Other Benefits
heading: F.5 No Other Benefits :
start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee shall not be entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan while he is a Covered U.K. Employee (or while he would be a Covered U.K. Employee if clauses (iv) and (v) of Section F .2. were not included in the definition of Covered U.K. Employee).
summary:
- Coordination of benefits for Covered U.K. Employees: If a Covered U.K. Employee has already earned a benefit under Article F, reaches the U.S. Cessation Date, and then works for PepsiCo in a role eligible under other plan provisions, any new benefit under those provisions is calculated for the new service but reduced by the lump-sum value of the prior Article F benefit to avoid duplication.
- Exclusivity and company discretion (F.5): While someone is a Covered U.K. Employee, they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan. Before all requirements to be a Covered U.K. Employee are met, there is no legally binding right to an Article F benefit. The Company may, in its unfettered discretion, take actions (e.g., not designating the individual as a Covered U.K. Employee) that prevent entitlement, regardless of services rendered.
- Appendix G (Delay Election for Certain Pre-2018 Terminees): Establishes a one-time opportunity, effective January 1, 2018, for Participants who separated before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension to delay distribution under Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
- Eligibility for Delay Election (G.2): Must have separated before January 1, 2018; have a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election date; and be selected and notified by the Company in its sole discretion.
- Requirements for Delay Election (G.3): Election must become effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the existing Scheduled Payment Date, and the new payment date must be at least 5 years later than the original Scheduled Payment Date (with an upper limit not shown in the excerpt).

title: Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 Terminees
heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE G - Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 T erminees
start_phrase: This Article provides an opportunity for certain Participants, who Separated from Service before January 1, 2018 and who are eligible to receive a 409A V ested Pension, to make a one-time election to delay the distribution of their 409A V ested Pension as permitted by Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
summary:
- Appendix G establishes a one-time “Delay Election” for Participants who separated from service before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension, allowing them to defer distribution under Code section 409A(a)(4)(C), effective January 1, 2018.
- Eligibility requires: (a) separation before January 1, 2018; (b) a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election date; and (c) selection and notice by the Company in its sole discretion.
- Election requirements: it must be irrevocable at least 12 months before the original Scheduled Payment Date and set a New Scheduled Payment Date at least five years later, but no later than the first of the month on or after the Participant’s 65th birthday.
- The election cannot change the payment form; however, the annuity form is determined by marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date, and any early commencement reduction is recalculated by reference to the New Scheduled Payment Date.
- Cashout provisions in Section 4.9 continue to apply even if a Delay Election is made.
- Appendix H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for periods prior to January 1, 2019: from January 1, 2016 through December 31, 2018 the Plan does not recognize Eligible Domestic Partner status due to the Supreme Court’s 2015 same-sex marriage ruling, with a limited 2016 exception for Participants who had a qualifying domestic partner or civil union as of December 31, 2015 and met specified employment/participant criteria in 2015.
- It also begins rules for June 26, 2013 through December 31, 2015, including recognition of civil unions in states that did not permit same-sex marriage (details partially shown).

APPENDIX ARTICLE G -
Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 T erminees     
G.1    Scope :
This Article provides an opportunity for certain Participants, who Separated from Service before January 1,
2018 and who are eligible to receive a 409A V ested Pension, to make a one-time election to delay the distribution of
their 409A V ested Pension as permitted by Code section 409A(a)(4)(C). This opportunity is referred to in this
Appendix G as a Delay Election. This Article is ef fective as of January 1, 2018.
G.2    Eligibility for Making a Delay Election .
To be eligible to make a Delay Election, a Participant must:
(a)    Have Separated from Service before January 1, 2018,
(b)    Be eligible for a 409A V ested Pension for which the scheduled payment date under the regular
terms of the Plan, as determined by the Plan Administrator , (the “Scheduled Payment Date”) is at least 12
months after the date the Participant will make the election, and
(c)    Be selected and notified by the Company , in its sole discretion, for the opportunity to make a Delay
Election.
G.3    Requirements for Making a Delay Election
To be ef fective, a request for a Delay Election must:
(a)    Become fully ef fective and irrevocable at least 12 months in advance of the Scheduled Payment
Date that was previously in ef fect, and
(b)    Specify a new scheduled date for payment commencement that is at least 5 years later than the
Participant’ s Scheduled Payment Date (but that is not later
- 132 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthan the first of the month coincident with or immediately following the Participant’ s 65th birthday) (the “New
Scheduled Payment Date”).
G.4    No Change in Form
A Participant is not permitted to use a Delay Election to change the form of payment of his or her distribution,
except that:
(a)    The Participant’ s marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date shall determine the form
of annuity payable under the Delay Election (with such marital status determined as of the New Scheduled
Payment Date in accordance with Section 6.3(c) (“Determination of Marital Status”)), and
(b)    Any reduction for early commencement (as applicable under Section 5.1(b) (“Basis for
Determining”)) of the benefit, which is subject to the Delay Election, shall be determined with reference to the
New Scheduled Payment Date.
G.5    Cashout Provisions Not Superseded .
A benefit to which an ef fective Delay Election applies remains subject to the cashout distribution provisions in
Section 4.9.

title: Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019
heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE H – Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019
start_phrase: This Article H provides the definition of Eligible Domestic Partner for periods prior to January 1, 2019.
summary:
- Appendix Article H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for periods before January 1, 2019, with time-specific rules:
  - Jan 1, 2016–Dec 31, 2018: Domestic partner status not recognized due to nationwide same-sex marriage; limited exception for 2016 for participants who had a qualifying same-sex domestic partner or civil union in place on Dec 31, 2015 and were active/on leave/participants during 2015.
  - June 26, 2013–Dec 31, 2015: For residents of states without same-sex marriage:
    - If the state allows same-sex civil unions: eligibility only if in a valid same-sex civil union.
    - If the state allows neither same-sex marriage nor civil unions: eligibility only if there is a legally binding same-sex domestic partner agreement meeting company requirements.
  - Jan 1, 2013–June 25, 2013: Recognizes spouses in valid same-sex marriages; residents of states permitting same-sex marriage can have an Eligible Domestic Partner only if married or if the state began permitting such marriages less than 12 months before the applicable date.
  - Pre-2013: No Eligible Domestic Partner status.
  - Additional rules: Opposite-sex partners never qualify; residents of states permitting same-sex marriage cannot have an Eligible Domestic Partner (must marry); a 12-month transition applies when a state newly permits marriage or civil unions. Defined terms: “applicable date” is the earlier of annuity start date or death; “state” includes domestic or foreign jurisdictions that sanction marriages or civil unions.

- Appendix Article I establishes a 409A Program makeup benefit for certain Pre-409A Participants:
  - Scope: Avoids “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program by not changing its early commencement actuarial factors; instead provides a makeup aligned with the 2019 Salaried Program Factors. For those already in the 409A Program, the makeup is provided under the main plan; this Article covers affected Pre-409A participants not otherwise eligible under the 409A Program.
  - Eligibility: Applies to Pre-409A Participants receiving a Vested Pension annuity starting before Normal Retirement Date on or after Jan 1, 2019, with the annuity reduced for early commencement under Pre-409A terms (additional criteria follow in the text).

Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019     
H.1    Scope .

Paragraphs a, b, c and d are ef fective for the dates indicated in the paragraph. Paragraph e sets forth general

title: 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE I – 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
start_phrase: To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the definition of Actuarial Equivalent).
summary:
- Appendix Article I – 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre‑409A Benefits:
  - Purpose/Scope: Provides a 409A Program “make‑up” benefit to avoid materially modifying the Pre‑409A Program by updating early retirement factors; instead, it compensates certain Pre‑409A Participants for harsher early commencement reductions relative to the 2019 Salaried Program Factors. Applies here only to affected Pre‑409A Participants who otherwise are not entitled to a 409A benefit.
  - Eligibility: Must be a Pre‑409A Participant receiving a Vested Pension annuity that starts before Normal Retirement Date on/after January 1, 2019; whose early commencement reduction under the Pre‑409A Program is greater than it would be using the 2019 Salaried Program Factors; and who otherwise has no 409A Pension payable on/after January 1, 2019 (or whose 409A Pension began before that date). Such individuals are “Eligible Persons.”
  - Benefit Amount: A single lump sum equal to the Actuarial Equivalent of the difference between (a) the Single Life Annuity using the 2019 Salaried Program Factors (including any PEP Guarantee portion) and (b) the actual Single Life Annuity using the pre‑2019 factors (including any PEP Guarantee portion). If the applicable commencement date is December 1, 2019 and the Annuity Starting Date was earlier, the value is determined at the actual start date and brought forward with Actuarial Equivalent interest to December 1, 2019. Only the factors effective January 1, 2019 apply.
  - Time of Payment: Payable as of the latest of (a) the first of the month after Separation from Service, (b) December 1, 2019, or (c) the first of the month after age 55 (not applicable to Article PBG‑derived benefits). If payment is delayed under Section 6.6(a) of the Plan, interest is added for the delay under Section 6.6(c).
  - Non‑Duplication: The makeup is reduced to eliminate any duplication if a participant has or will receive a 409A Pension that already provides some/all of the makeup (e.g., via early retirement reduction factors) or if the Plan Administrator determines duplication would occur; this rule overrides any contrary provision.

- Appendix Article J – Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons (partial):
  - Scope: Establishes special benefit and distribution rules (to be detailed in Sections J.3 and J.4) for “Covered International Employees.”
  - Definitions: A “Covered International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who (1) is ineligible for PERP, (2) would be barred from earning PIRP‑DB benefits under Section 9.14 of PIRP‑DB due to U.S. Person status, (3) is initially selected by the Vice President based on special retirement‑benefit circumstances, and (4) is subsequently determined by the Vice President to be entitled to this status. Both determinations are in the Vice President’s unfettered discretion. (Further benefit and distribution details not included in the excerpt.)
text:
APPENDIX ARTICLE I –
409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
    
    I.1    Scope:
To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a
makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-
409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of
Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the
definition of Actuarial Equivalent). In the case of participants in the Pre-409A Program who are also
Participants in the 409A Program (without regard to this Article), this makeup relating to the early
commencement reduction of V ested Pensions payable as annuities is provided under the main text of the
Plan. However , this makeup is provided under this Article in the case of af fected Pre-409A Participants who
are otherwise not entitled to a benefit under the 409A Program.
I.2    Eligibility Under This Article :
To be eligible under this Article, an individual must be a Pre-409A Participant:
(a)    Who is paid a Pre-409A Pension that is (i) a “V ested Pension” under the Pre-409A Program, and
(ii) paid in the form of an annuity commencing as of a date prior to the Pre-409A Participant’ s Normal
Retirement Date but as of on or after January 1, 2019;
(b)     Whose Pre-409A Pension annuity under subsection (a) above is reduced for early
commencement under the terms of the Pre-409A Program by more
- 137 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthan it would be if the early commencement reduction were calculated using the 2019 Salaried Plan
Factors; and
(c)    Who otherwise would not have a 409A Pension that is payable ef fective as of January 1, 2019 or
later because, except as provided in this Article, the only PEP Pension to which the individual is entitled
is a Pre-409A Pension, or because his otherwise applicable 409A Pension commenced payment as of
prior to January 1, 2019.
An individual who satisfies all of the foregoing eligibility requirements shall be referred to as an “Eligible
Person” for purposes of this Article.
I.3    Benefit Amount Under This Article :
The benefit amount for an Eligible Person under this Article shall be the single lump sum that is the
Actuarial Equivalent of the dif ference between:
(a)    The Single Life Annuity that would be payable to the Eligible Person under the Pre-409A Program
as of the Eligible Person’ s Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program if the 2019 Salaried
Program Factors for early commencement applied in calculating such Single Life Annuity (including with
respect to any portion of the Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension that is derived from the PEP Guarantee),
and
(b)    The Single Life Annuity that is actually applicable to the Eligible Person under the Pre-409A
Program as of the Eligible Person’ s Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program, because of the
early commencement factors that
- 138 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programare actually applicable in calculating such Single Life Annuity (including with respect to any portion of
the Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension that is derived from the PEP Guarantee).
Such Actuarial Equivalent lump sum shall be calculated as of the applicable commencement date specified in
Section I.4 below; however , if the applicable commencement date is the Section I.4(b) date ( i.e. December 1,
2019) and the Eligible Person’ s actual Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program precedes December
1, 2019, then the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum shall be determined as of such actual Annuity Starting Date
and then brought forward with Actuarial Equivalent interest to December 1, 2019. For purposes of subsection
(a) above, the 2019 Salaried Program Factors shall be solely the new factors applicable under the Salaried
Program as of January 1, 2019 (and no alternative calculation using the factors in ef fect before January 1,
2019 shall apply).
I.4    Time of Payment Under This Article :
The lump sum benefit calculated under this Appendix shall be payable as of the Eligible Person’ s
applicable commencement date, which is the latest of the following:
(a)     The first of the month following the Eligible Person’ s Separation from Service,
(b)     December 1, 2019, or
- 139 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(c)     The first of the month following the Eligible Person’ s attainment of age 55 (except that this
subsection (c) shall not apply to the extent that the Eligible Person’ s benefit is derived from Article PBG
of this Appendix).
In the event that the Eligible Person’ s applicable commencement date is the date in subsection (a) above, then
the date of actual payment of the benefit shall be delayed to the extent provided by Section 6.6(a) of the main
text of the Plan, and in the case of such a delay , the benefit determined as of such applicable commencement
date shall be increased by interest for the period of delay as provided in Section 6.6(c) of the main text of the
Plan.
I.5    Non-Duplication of Benefits :
The foregoing Sections of this Article are intended to provide a make-up benefit under the 409A Program for applying
an early commencement reduction under the Pre-409A Program using factors that predate the 2019 Salaried Plan
Factors, with respect to a Pre-409A Pension that is paid in the form of an annuity and that has an Annuity Starting
Date of January 1, 2019 or later . However , no duplication of benefits may occur at any time under the Plan.
Therefore, to the extent an Eligible Person has received or will receive a 409A Pension that, without regard to this
Article, ef fectively provides some or all of such makeup ( e.g., because the Eligible Person’ s 409A Pension was
reduced for early commencement using Early Retirement reduction factors), or to the extent that the Plan
Administrator concludes that providing the makeup under this Article would otherwise result in a duplication of
benefits, the makeup benefit under this Article shall be reduced (but not below zero) as the Plan Administrator deems
appropriate to eliminate all
- 140 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programduplication of benefits. This provision shall govern over any contrary provision of this Article or the Plan that might be
interpreted to support a duplication of benefits.

PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program

heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE J - Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons
start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below .
summary: This section introduces Article J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, defining scope and key terms for “Covered International Employees” who are U.S. Persons. It applies to employees of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate (non-U.S. entity designated by the Vice President) who are ineligible for PERP, would be barred from PIRP-DB benefits under Section 9.14 due to U.S. Person status, are initially selected by the Vice President based on special circumstances, and are subsequently determined—at the Vice President’s unfettered discretion—to be Covered International Employees. It clarifies that before this determination (made in conjunction with the employee’s retirement and not before the year of the Section J.4 distribution date), a Selected International Employee has no legally binding right to a pension or distribution under Code Sections 409A and 457A. It references that benefits are determined under Section J.3 and distributed under Section J.4, and defines PERP, PIRP-DB, U.S. Person, and the Vice President role as used in PIRP-DB.
text:
Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons     
J.1    Scope :
This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below . The benefit of a
Covered International Employee shall be determined as provided in Section J.3 below . A benefit determined for a
Covered International Employee under this Article shall be distributed as provided in Section J.4 below .
J.2    Definitions :
    Where the following words and phrases appear in this Article J with initial capital letters, they shall have the
meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
(a)    A “Covered International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Af filiate, who—
(1)    Is ineligible to participate in PERP ,
(2)    W ould be barred from earning a benefit under PIRP-DB by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB (based
on the employee’ s status as a U.S. Person),
(3)    Is initially selected by the V ice President as eligible to be a Covered International Employee
based on the existence of special circumstances regarding his ability to receive retirement benefits, and
(4)    Is subsequently determined by the V ice President to be entitled to status as a Covered
International Employee.
The selection in paragraph (3) above and the determination in paragraph (4) above shall be made in the
unfettered discretion of the V ice President. In addition, the
- 142 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program
determination in paragraph (4) shall be made in conjunction with a Selected International Employee’ s
Retirement (but not before the year of a Selected International Employee’ s distribution date under Section J.4).
Prior to the time of the determination in paragraph (4) above, a Selected International Employee shall not have
a legally binding right (within the meaning of Code Sections 409A and 457A) to a Pension or any distribution
under this Article J.
(b)    A “Designated PepsiCo Af filiate” is an employing entity that (i) is organized under the laws of a
country other than the United States, and (ii) has been designated by the V ice President as eligible to have its
employees covered by this Article J.
(c)    “PERP” means the PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan A, PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan
I, PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan H or any predecessor or successor plan to one or more of the
foregoing.
(d)    “PIRP-DB” means the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan (DB Program).
(e)    A “Selected International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Af filiate who
satisfies paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) of subsection (a) above, but who has not yet been determined to be
entitled under paragraph (4) of subsection (a) above.
(e)    A “U.S. Person” is an individual who is classified as a “U.S. Person” under the terms of PIRP-DB.
(f)    The “V ice President” is the Company executive who has the role of the “V ice President” under the
terms of PIRP-DB.

start_phrase: A Covered International Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating the Pension to which he would be entitled under the main part of the Plan (which shall include treating the Covered International Employee as a Plan Participant and reflecting the dif ferences in the calculation of a Participant’ s Pension that is a Vested Pension versus a Retirement Pension), but giving ef fect to the following modifications.
summary:

- Benefit calculation: Determined under the main Plan as if the employee is a Plan Participant, accounting for Vested vs. Retirement Pension differences, with specific modifications.

start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation of a Covered International Employee’ s Pension under this Appendix J.
summary:
- Outlines operating rules for calculating a Covered International Employee’s Pension under Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Requires Single Lump Sum calculations to use actuarial assumptions compliant with Internal Revenue Code Section 417(e), specifically the same assumptions the Salaried Plan would use as of the lump-sum determination date.
- Confirms the pension is fully subject to the Salaried Plan freeze effective December 31, 2025, with all accruals, rights, and benefits frozen to the same extent as under the Salaried Plan.
- States in Section J.6 (No Other Benefits) that while an individual is a Designated or Covered International Employee, they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB, or any termination indemnity arrangement.

start_phrase: Effective as of the end of the day on December 31, 2011, the PBG PEP is hereby merged with and into the PepsiCo PEP, with the PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan after the merger .
summary: Introduces Appendix Article PBG following the merger of the PBG PEP into the PepsiCo PEP effective December 31, 2011, with PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan; states that this appendix governs PBG PEP benefits previously subject to the 409A PBG PEP Document, except that Articles VII (Administration), VIII (Miscellaneous), IX (Amendment and Termination), X (ERISA Plan Structure), and XI (Applicable Law) of the main document apply, and for Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019, actuarial adjustments from a Single Life Annuity to optional annuities (e.g., survivor, period certain, death benefit, or with other features) are determined under the main document; confirms no change to the time or form of payment of benefits subject to Code Section 409A due to the merger or incorporation revisions.

APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG     
Effective as of the end of the day on December 31, 2011, the PBG PEP is hereby merged with and into the PepsiCo

Law) of the main section of this document shall govern PBG PEP benefits that were subject to the 409A PBG PEP

period certain annuity or other death benefit annuity (or an annuity with other optional features), the adjustment of the

Code section 409A under either the PepsiCo PEP or PBG PEP Document as a result of the plan merger or the

title: HISTORY AND PURPOSE
heading: ARTICLE I T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - HIST ORY AND PURPOSE
start_phrase: The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. (“PBG”) established the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) ef fective April 6, 1999 for the benefit of salaried employees of the PBG Organization who participate in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan (“Salaried Plan”).
summary:
- Effective Dec 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) is merged into the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PepsiCo PEP), with PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan.
- This Appendix governs PBG PEP benefits that were subject to the 409A PBG PEP Document before the merger, except:
  - Administration, Miscellaneous, Amendment and Termination, ERISA Plan Structure, and Applicable Law are governed by the main PepsiCo PEP document (Articles VII–XI).
  - For Annuity Starting Dates on or after Jan 1, 2019, actuarial adjustments for optional annuities (e.g., survivor, period certain, death benefit) follow the main document.
- The merger and incorporation of the 409A PBG PEP provisions do not change the time or form of payments for benefits subject to Code section 409A under either plan.
- History and purpose:
  - PBG established the PBG PEP on Apr 6, 1999 (post-IPO) as a successor to the PepsiCo PEP for salaried employees in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan.
  - Provides supplemental benefits where qualified plan benefits are limited by the Internal Revenue Code and for certain employees under the pre-1989 formula.
  - Effective Apr 1, 2009, covers pay reductions from deferrals under the PBG Executive Income Deferral Program and certain executives (salary bands E3–E8 or MP) who would otherwise be grandfathered under the Salaried Plan.
  - Intended as a nonqualified, unfunded deferred compensation plan; for ERISA, split into:
    - An “excess benefit plan” (ERISA §4(b)(5)) for Code §415 limitations.
    - A “top-hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 301(a)(3), 401(a)(1)).
  - Amended multiple times, including a full restatement effective Apr 1, 2009; further amended following the 2009 merger to facilitate PepsiCo’s assumption as plan sponsor.
- Effect of amendment and restatement:
  - Defines the Prior Plan as the plan in effect on Oct 3, 2004 and the “Grandfathered Benefit” as the benefit determined as if termination occurred Dec 31, 2004, paid in the time and form under the Oct 3, 2004 terms.
  - Post-2004 accruals (net of the Grandfathered Benefit) are paid per the current plan.
  - The current plan superseded the Prior Plan effective Jan 1, 2009 for amounts accrued and vested after 2004 for participants not in pay status as of that date.
  - From 2005–2008, the plan was administered in good faith compliance with Code §409A; post-2004 amounts are treated as a separate plan for §409A purposes.
- Definitions and construction:
  - Terms used have the meanings set in this Plan; unless otherwise specified, terms align with those in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan.

ARTICLE I T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - HIST ORY AND PURPOSE
1.1    History of Plan . The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. (“PBG”) established the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP”
or “Plan”) ef fective April 6, 1999 for the benefit of salaried employees of the PBG Organization who participate in the
PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan (“Salaried Plan”). The Plan was initially established as a successor plan to
the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan, due to PBG’ s April 6, 1999 initial public of fering, and the Plan included
historical PepsiCo provisions which are relevant for eligibility and benefit determinations under the Plan. The Plan
provides benefits for eligible employees whose pension benefits under the
- 147 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramSalaried Plan are limited by the provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. In addition, the Plan
provides benefits for certain eligible employees based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula. Effective April 1, 2009,
the Plan also provides benefits for employees whose eligible pay under the Salaried Plan is reduced due to the
employees’ elective deferrals under the PBG Executive Income Deferral Program and for certain executives who
would be “Grandfathered Participants” under the Salaried Plan but for their classification as salary band E3-E8 or MP
(or its equivalent, for periods on and after the Ef fective T ime). The Plan is intended as a nonqualified unfunded
deferred compensation plan for federal income tax purposes. For purposes of the Employee Retirement Income
Security Act of 1974 (“ERISA”), the Plan is structured as two plans. The portion of the Plan that provides benefits
based on limitations imposed by Section 415 of the Internal Revenue Code (the “Code”) is intended to be an “excess
benefit plan” as described in Section 4(b)(5) of ERISA. The remainder of the Plan is intended to be a plan described
in Sections 201(2), 301(a)(3) and 401(a)(1) of ERISA providing benefits to a select group of management or highly-
compensated employees.
The Plan has been amended from time to time, most recently in the form of an amendment and complete restatement
effective as of April 1, 2009 (“2009 Restatement”). PBG further amended the Plan as a result of the merger of PBG
with and into Pepsi-Cola Metropolitan Bottling Company , Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of PepsiCo, Inc. (the
“Company”), pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated as of August 3, 2009 among PBG, the Company
and Pepsi-Cola Metropolitan Company , Inc., and to facilitate the Company’ s assumption of PBG’ s role as the Plan’ s
sponsor .
1.2    Effect of Amendment and Restatement . The Plan as in ef fect on October 3, 2004 is referred to herein as the
Prior Plan.
- 148 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramExcept as otherwise explicitly provided in Section 6.1(b)(3) of this Plan, a Participant’ s benefit (including death
benefits), determined under the terms of the Plan as in ef fect on October 3, 2004 as if the Participant had terminated
employment on December 31, 2004, without regard to any compensation paid or services rendered after 2004, or any
other events af fecting the amount of or the entitlement to benefits (other than the Participant’ s survival or the
Participant’ s election under the terms of the Plan with respect to the time or form of benefit) (the “Grandfathered
Benefit”) shall be paid at the time and in the form provided by the terms of the Plan as in ef fect on October 3, 2004.
The benefit of a Participant accrued under this Plan based on all compensation and services taken into account by
the Prior Plan and this Plan, less the Participant’ s Grandfathered Benefit, shall be paid in the times and in the form as
provided in this Plan. Except as otherwise explicitly provided in this Plan, this Plan superseded the Prior Plan
effective January 1, 2009, with respect to amounts accrued and vested after 2004 by Participants who had not
commenced receiving benefits as of January 1, 2009. The Plan was administered in accordance with a good faith
interpretation of Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code and IRS regulations and guidance thereunder from
January 1, 2005 through December 31, 2008. Amounts accrued under this Plan after 2004 shall be treated as
payable under a separate Plan for purposes of Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.

title: DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
heading: ARTICLE II T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
start_phrase: The following words and phrases, when used in this Plan, shall have the meaning set forth below unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.
summary:
- Establishes “Grandfathered Benefit” treatment: benefits determined under plan terms in effect on October 3, 2004 as if employment ended December 31, 2004, disregarding post‑2004 compensation or events (other than survival/elections), to be paid in the time and form provided under the 2004 plan terms.
- Provides that non‑grandfathered benefits (total accrued under Prior Plan and this Plan minus the Grandfathered Benefit) are payable under this Plan’s time/form rules; the Plan superseded the Prior Plan effective January 1, 2009 for amounts accrued and vested after 2004 for participants not yet in pay status.
- Describes Section 409A compliance history: administered in good faith with 409A from 2005–2008; amounts accrued after 2004 treated as a separate plan for 409A purposes.
- Defines key terms and structure (Article II), including:
  - Actuarial Equivalent; Annuity; Code; ERISA; Plan, PepsiCo Prior Plan, and Plan Administrator (PepsiCo Administration Committee); Effective Date (April 6, 1999) and Effective Time (February 26, 2010); Company (PepsiCo, Inc.; previously The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. before the Effective Time).
  - Compensation Limitation (Code §401(a)(17)) and Section 415 Limitation; Salaried Plan (Part C governs); Salaried Plan Participant; Employer; Employee; Participant.
  - PepsiCo/PBG Organization (controlled group under Code §414).
  - PEP Pension and Grandfathered Benefit; Single Lump Sum (for the portion in excess of Grandfathered Benefit).
  - Separation from Service; Section 409A; Plan Year.
  - Primary Social Security Amount assumptions and exclusions for pension calculations (assumes wages at the taxable wage base until retirement/severance; special rule for vested pensions; excludes spouse/dependent and post‑severance adjustments; measured as of Severance from Service Date).
  - Vested Pension.
- Provides comprehensive “Specified Employee” identification rules for 409A (officers/owners thresholds; annual December 31 determination effective the following April 1; administrative convenience rule treating E5+ as specified employees subject to a 200‑person cap; special transition combining lists Feb 26–Mar 31, 2010; post‑April 1, 2010 method using Band IV/E7/Salary Grade 19 classifications with caps; intended as an alternative method under Treas. Reg. §1.409A‑1(i)(5)).
- Sets construction rules (gender/number usage; “hereof/hereunder” refer to entire Plan).
- Defines participation eligibility (Article III): all Salaried Plan Participants whose benefits are limited by §401(a)(17) or §415; specified groups tied to Grandfathered status and elective deferrals to the Executive Income Deferral Program during 4/1/2009–12/31/2010 (with special treatment for certain E3–E8 or MP classifications as of 3/31/2009); and those with 1988 pensionable earnings of $75,000 or more.

title: PARTICIPATION
heading: ARTICLE III T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - P ARTICIP ATION
start_phrase: Each Salaried Plan Participant whose benefit under the Salaried Plan is curtailed by the Compensation Limitation or the Section 415 Limitation, or both, and each other Salaried Plan Participant (i) who is a Grandfathered Employee as defined in Section 3.7 of the Salaried Plan and who made elective deferrals to the EID on or after April 1, 2009 and before January 1, 2011 (inclusively); (ii) who would have been considered a Grandfathered Participant as defined in Section 3.7 of the Salaried Plan during the period April 1, 2009 through December 31, 2010 if the Participant had not been classified by the Employer as salary band E3-E8 or MP on March 31, 2009; or (iii) whose 1988 pensionable “earnings” under the Salaried Plan, as described in Section 4.2(a), were $75,000 or more, shall participate in this Plan.
summary:
- Excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program defining key terms and calculation rules.
- Defines “Vested Pension” as the PEP benefit for a participant who is vested but not eligible for a Retirement Pension.
- Sets plan construction rules: gender-neutral usage, singular/plural flexibility, and that “hereof,” “hereunder,” etc., refer to the entire plan.
- Establishes participation eligibility for certain Salaried Plan Participants, including those whose Salaried Plan benefits are limited by the Compensation Limitation or IRC Section 415 limits; specified “Grandfathered” groups tied to elective deferrals to the EID between April 1, 2009 and December 31, 2010; those who would have been Grandfathered but for classification as salary band E3–E8 or MP on March 31, 2009; and those with 1988 pensionable earnings of $75,000 or more.

summary: Defines how a Participant’s PEP Pension is determined under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program as of Separation from Service, subject to Sections 4.5 and 8.7. If paid in the same form/time as the Salaried Plan, the monthly PEP equals the excess of the greater of (i) the hypothetical Salaried Plan benefit ignoring the Compensation Limitation, IRC §415 limit, the exclusion of elective deferrals under the EID between April 1, 2009 and January 1, 2011, and the 2009–2010 exclusion from the Salaried Plan’s Grandfathered Participant definition for certain E3–E8/MP employees meeting age/service thresholds, or (ii) any Section 4.2 amount, over the actual Salaried Plan benefit, payable per Section 6.2 net of the Grandfathered Benefit. If paid in a different form/time, the PEP equals the greater-of amount (or Section 4.2 amount in the PEP form/time) multiplied by a fraction: (greater-of value minus Salaried Plan value) divided by the greater-of value, with values determined on a reasonable and consistent basis at the Plan Administrator’s discretion for similarly situated employees; payable per Section 6.2 net of the Grandfathered Benefit. title: PEP Guarantee Formula
heading: (b) PEP Guarantee Formula .
start_phrase:
The amount of a Participant’ s PEP Guarantee shall be determined
under paragraph (1), subject to the special rules in paragraph (2).
summary:
- Sets the PEP Guarantee formula:
  - 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus
  - 1% of HAME for each year of Credited Service over 10, minus
  - 1 2/3% of the Primary Social Security Amount times Credited Service (capped at 30 years).

- Describes vested pension methodology:
  - First, project Credited Service to Normal Retirement Age and use HAME and Primary Social Security Amount at the earlier of Severance from Service or accrual cessation.
  - Then prorate by the ratio of actual Credited Service to projected Credited Service to Normal Retirement Age.

- Special calculation rules:
  - Survivor benefit for Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner: 50% of the Participant’s annuity with no reduction to the Participant’s annuity; if the survivor is over 10 years younger, reduce by 0.8% per full year ages 11–20 and an additional 0.4% per full year beyond 20; applies to those retiring on/after Early Retirement Date.
  - Early retirement reduction: 3/12 of 1% per month benefits commence before Normal Retirement Date.
  - Vested Pension commencing before Normal Retirement Date: convert to Actuarial Equivalent; apply Salaried Plan reductions for Pre-Retirement Spouse/Domestic Partner coverage.
  - If electing:
    - A form with greater surviving spouse/partner benefits than the standard 50%,
    - A survivor annuity for a non-eligible beneficiary, or
    - An annuity with inflation protection,
    then reduce the PEP Guarantee so the total value equals the Actuarial Equivalent of the standard form (e.g., Single Life Annuity or elected annuity without inflation protection, as applicable).
  - Lump sum distribution: convert PEP Guarantee to its Actuarial Equivalent, factoring in survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.

- April 1, 2009 Salaried Plan changes:
  - Certain employees (salary bands E3–E8 or MP) who as of March 31, 2009 were age 50 with 5 years of Service or had age + Service ≥ 65 are treated as Grandfathered for April 1, 2009–December 31, 2010 (Earnings and Credited Service not frozen).
  - HAME disregards exclusions for EID elective deferrals made between April 1, 2009 and December 31, 2010.

- Notes upcoming Section 4.3: benefits are subject to additional adjustments; defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or a similar nonqualified pension plan sponsored by a PBG member.

title: Certain Adjustments
heading: 4.3 Certain Adjustments .
start_phrase:
Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to
adjustment as provided in this section.
summary:
- Explains how the PEP Guarantee is converted to a lump sum as the actuarial equivalent of the annuity, factoring in survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.
- Details special April 1, 2009 Salaried Plan provisions:
  - Certain E3–E8/MP participants meeting age/service thresholds (age 50 with 5 years, or age + service ≥ 65) are treated as Grandfathered Participants from April 1, 2009, so Earnings and Credited Service were not frozen through December 31, 2010.
  - Highest Average Monthly Earnings are calculated without excluding participant EID deferrals made from April 1, 2009 to December 31, 2010.
- Defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified pension plans within the PBG organization whose benefits are not based on participant deferrals, including the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
- Provides adjustment rules:
  - Rehired participants: If the Salaried Plan benefit is (or would have been) recalculated for additional Credited Service after the annuity start date, the PEP Pension is recalculated, with adjustments for prior/in‑service distributions and coordination with specified plans.
  - Increases in benefits under specified plans after PEP determination trigger a PEP recalculation; overpayments may be recovered; no duplication of benefits is intended.
  - Offsets are limited to avoid changes in time or form of payment prohibited by Section 409A; the Company may arrange 409A‑compliant coordination under qualifying plans to permit offsets without violating 409A.
- Addresses reemployment: Non‑Grandfathered PEP Pension payments continue during reemployment; any additional PEP accrued after reemployment will be reduced at subsequent separation by the present value of prior PEP payments.
- States vesting: A participant’s PEP Accrued Benefit vests when the participant vests under the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 and further plan provisions (text incomplete).

3    Certain Adjustments . Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to
adjustment as provided in this section. For purposes of this section, “specified plan” shall mean the Salaried Plan or a
nonqualified pension plan similar to this Plan. A nonqualified pension plan is similar to this Plan if it is sponsored by a
member of the PBG
