PepsiCo Prior Plan).
(a)    Adjustments for Rehired Participants . This subsection shall apply to a current or former
Participant who is reemployed after his Annuity Starting Date and (i) whose benefit under the Salaried Plan is
recalculated based on an additional period of Credited Service, or (ii) whose benefit under the Salaried Plan
would have been recalculated, based on an additional period of Credited Service if the Participant would have
been considered a Grandfathered Participant as defined in Section 3.7 of the Salaried Plan if the Participant
was not classified by the Employer as salary band E3-E8 or MP . In such event, the Participant’ s PEP Pension
shall be recalculated hereunder . For this purpose, the PEP Guarantee under Section 4.2 is adjusted for in-
service distributions and prior distributions in the same manner as benefits are adjusted under the Salaried
Plan, but by taking into account benefits under this Plan and any specified plans.
(b)    Adjustment for Increased Pension Under Other Plans . If the benefit paid under a specified plan
on behalf of a Participant is increased after PEP benefits on his behalf have been determined (whether the
increase is by order of a court, by agreement of the plan administrator of the specified plan, or otherwise), the
PEP benefit for the Participant shall be recalculated. If the recalculation identifies an overpayment hereunder ,
the Plan Administrator shall take such steps as it deems advisable to recover the overpayment. It is specifically
intended that there shall be no duplication of payments under this Plan and any specified plans.
(c)    No Benefit Offsets That W ould V iolate Section 409A . If a Participant has earned a benefit under
a plan maintained by a member of the PepsiCo/PBG

Salaried Plan and the “T ransfers and Non-Duplication” rule in Section 3.6 of Part C of the Salaried Plan, such
Transfers and Non-Duplication rules shall apply when calculating the amount determined under Section 4.1(a)
(1) or 4.1(b)(1) above (as applicable) only to the extent the application of such rule will not result in a change in
the time or form of payment of such pension that is prohibited by Section 409A. For purposes of the limit on

title: Vesting; Misconduct
heading: 4.5 Vesting; Misconduct .
start_phrase:
Subject to Section 8.7, a Participant shall be fully vested in his Accrued Benefit at
the time he becomes fully vested in his accrued benefit under the Salaried Plan.
summary:
- Coordination with Salaried Plan non-duplication/transfer rules: Offsets under the Salaried Plan’s Non-Duplication provisions apply to PEP Pension calculations only to the extent they do not change the time or form of payment in a way prohibited by Section 409A. The Company intends to implement 409A-compliant special arrangements under qualifying plans to avoid such changes; when such arrangements are in place, the offset limits do not apply.
- Reemployment after annuity starting date: Payments of a non-Grandfathered PEP Pension are not suspended upon reemployment. If additional PEP benefits accrue after reemployment, the subsequent PEP Pension is reduced by the present value of previously paid PEP benefits.
- Vesting and misconduct: Vesting in the PEP mirrors vesting under the Salaried Plan (subject to Section 8.7). A participant forfeits the entire PEP Pension if the Plan Administrator, in good faith, finds “Misconduct,” regardless of whether it occurred before or after severance. The Plan Administrator may also require repayment of PEP amounts paid within the prior 12 months.
- Definition of “Misconduct”: Includes violations of agreements (e.g., confidentiality, non-solicit, non-compete), duties (including Code of Conduct), disparagement, misuse or disclosure of confidential information, unlawful trading/insider trading, actions against the Company’s best interests (including employee solicitation), and felonies or gross misconduct. Whistleblowing to government authorities is protected; attorney-client privilege is preserved.
- Death benefits: For participants who die before their annuity starting date, the death benefit equals what would have been payable under the Salaried Plan if the PEP applied there. The portion above the Grandfathered Benefit is paid as a single lump sum at death. Beneficiaries mirror the Salaried Plan, including eligible domestic partners for deaths on/after January 1, 2013.
- Distributions: Article VI governs the form and timing of PEP Pension distributions, subject to Section 6.5.

5    Vesting; Misconduct . Subject to Section 8.7, a Participant shall be fully vested in his Accrued Benefit at
the time he becomes fully vested in his accrued benefit under the Salaried Plan. Notwithstanding the preceding, or
any other provision of the Plan to the

Participant has engaged in “Misconduct” as defined below , determined without regard to whether the Misconduct
occurred before or after the Participant’ s Severance from Service. The Plan Administrator may , in its sole discretion,
require the Participant to pay to the Employer any PEP Pension paid to the Participant within the twelve month period
immediately preceding a date on which the Participant has engaged in such Misconduct, as determined by the Plan
Administrator .
“Misconduct” means any of the following, as determined by the Plan Administrator in good faith: (i) violation of
any agreement between the Company or Employer and the Participant, including but not limited to a violation relating
to the disclosure of confidential information or trade secrets, the solicitation of employees, customers, suppliers,
licensors or contractors, or the performance of competitive services, (ii) violation of any duty to the Company or
Employer , including but not limited to violation of the Company’ s Code of Conduct; (iii) making, or causing or
attempting to cause any other person to make, any statement (whether written, oral or electronic), or conveying any
information about the Company or Employer which is disparaging or which in any way reflects negatively upon the
Company or Employer unless required by law or pursuant to a Company or Employer policy; (iv) improperly
disclosing or otherwise misusing any confidential information regarding the Company or Employer; (v) unlawful
trading in the securities of the Company or of another company based on information garnered as a result of that
Participant’ s employment or other relationship with the Company; (vi) engaging in any act which is considered to be
contrary to the best interests of the Company or Employer , including but not limited to recruiting or soliciting
employees of the Employer; or (vii) commission of a felony or other serious crime or engaging in any activity

title: Death Benefits
heading: 5.1 Death Benefits .
start_phrase:
Each Participant entitled to a PEP Pension under this Plan who dies before his Annuity
Starting Date shall be entitled to a death benefit equal in amount to the additional death benefit to which the
Participant would have been entitled under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension as determined under Article IV was
payable under the Salaried Plan instead of this Plan.
summary:
- Clarifies that while certain conduct may constitute gross misconduct, the Plan does not restrict Participants from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations; the Company maintains attorney-client privilege over protected information.
- Article V (Appendix PBG) outlines pre-retirement death benefits for Participants entitled to a PEP Pension who die before their Annuity Starting Date:
  - The death benefit equals the additional death benefit that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension were paid there instead.
  - Any portion of the PEP Pension exceeding the Grandfathered Benefit is payable as a single lump sum on the date of death.
  - Benefits are paid to the same beneficiaries and in the same proportions as under the Salaried Plan, including Eligible Domestic Partners for deaths on or after January 1, 2013.

summary:
- Clarifies that certain conduct constitutes gross misconduct, but affirms participants’ right to communicate with government authorities about possible legal violations; preserves the Company’s attorney-client privilege.
- Article V (Death Benefits):
  - For participants entitled to a PEP Pension who die before their Annuity Starting Date, the death benefit equals the additional death benefit that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension were paid there.
  - The portion of the death benefit exceeding the Grandfathered Benefit is paid as a Single Lump Sum on the date of death.
  - Payments follow the beneficiary designations/proportions under the Salaried Plan, including Eligible Domestic Partners for pre-retirement deaths on or after January 1, 2013.
- Article VI (Distributions of PEP Pensions):
  - Section 6.1 Form and Timing:
    - Grandfathered Benefit: paid per plan terms in effect on October 3, 2004.
    - Non-Grandfathered Benefit: generally paid as a Single Lump Sum upon Separation from Service.
    - Special cases:
      - Certain vested pensions: participants who separated between Jan 1, 2005–Dec 31, 2008 and whose Annuity Starting Date had not occurred by Jan 1, 2009 receive a Single Lump Sum on Jan 1, 2009.
      - Annuity election: participants age 50 by Jan 1, 2009 who irrevocably elected an annuity by Dec 31, 2008 and who terminate on/after July 1, 2009 after meeting specified age/service milestones (age 55 + 10 years of service, or age 65 + 5 years) receive the elected annuity starting the first day of the month on/after Separation; otherwise, a Single Lump Sum at Separation applies.
      - 2008 reorganization: certain involuntary separations between Nov 1–Dec 19, 2008 (age 50–54, 10+ years of service, eligible under a letter agreement) receive a Single Lump Sum on the last day of the defined Transition Period.
      - Specified Employees (409A): six-month payment delay after Separation; suspended amounts accrue interest at the applicable lump-sum rate.
      - Actual payment date: paid as soon as administratively feasible, no later than end of the calendar year of the specified date or the 15th day of the third month thereafter; further delay permitted if calculation is impracticable beyond the participant’s control, with payment in the first practicable year.
  - Section 6.2 Special Rules for Survivor Options:
    - If a participant who made an annuity election under 6.1(b)(2) dies before Separation, the election is disregarded.
    - Participants may change the coannuitant for a Joint and Survivor Annuity prior to Separation and may change the beneficiary of a 10-Year Certain and Life Annuity at any time.
    - If death occurs after the election is effective but before non-Grandfathered payments commence, the election is honored; survivor benefits to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary begin the first day of the month following death; any back payments due are paid to the estate.

title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
heading: 6.2 Special Rules for Survivor Options .
start_phrase:
If a Participant makes an Annuity election described in Section
6.1(b)(2) and the Participant dies before his Separation from Service, the election shall be disregarded.
summary:
- Payment timing: Benefits due on dates specified in Articles V or VI must be paid as soon as administratively feasible, no later than the later of the end of the calendar year of the specified date or the 15th day of the third month following that date. Participants cannot choose the taxable year. Payment may be further delayed if calculation is impracticable due to events beyond the participant’s control, with payment in the first calendar year when practicable.

- Survivor option rules:
  - If a participant elected an annuity with a survivor option and dies before separation from service, the election is disregarded. The coannuitant for a Joint and Survivor Annuity can be changed any time before separation; the beneficiary for a Ten Years Certain and Life Annuity can be changed at any time.
  - If the participant dies after the election becomes effective but before the non-Grandfathered PEP Pension starts, the election is honored; survivor payments to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary begin the first day of the month after death; any back payments owed to the participant go to the estate.
  - For a Ten Years Certain and Life Annuity: if the participant dies after commencement, has no surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and fewer than 120 payments have been made, remaining payments go to the participant’s estate. If a beneficiary was receiving payments and dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
  - If the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner: a 100% survivor option cannot be elected with a beneficiary more than 10 years younger; a 75% survivor option cannot be elected with a beneficiary more than 19 years younger.

- Beneficiary designation: Participants electing a form with a survivor option must designate a beneficiary on a PEP Election Form; they may change or revoke the designation until the election is finally effective. Designations and changes must follow Plan Administrator rules and are not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.

- Article C governs pension treatment for employees transferring between the Company and PepsiCo, Inc. only for transfers occurring before February 26, 2010, and it supersedes the main Plan for these cases.
- Transfers to PepsiCo, Inc.: The PEP Pension is fixed as of the transfer date using Article IV rules, including applying the Salaried Plan offset whether or not that benefit moves to a PepsiCo qualified plan. The determined benefit is payable at Separation from Service per Article VI.
- Transfers from PepsiCo, Inc.: The PEP Pension is determined at Separation from Service per Article IV and reduced by any PepsiCo plan benefits based on overlapping credited service so the combined benefits do not exceed what the Participant would have received if always employed by the Company. For transfers on or after January 1, 2005, the benefit cannot be less than the Company-only benefit. The Plan Administrator may adjust calculations to carry out this intent.
- Appendix Article PAC sets guiding principles for appointing members of the PAC (benefit plan committee).
  - Eligibility: must be a PepsiCo Organization employee at Leadership Group 1 or higher, able to devote sufficient time, and act prudently and solely in participants’ and beneficiaries’ interests.
  - Experience: each member should have benefit plan/ERISA administration experience (or comparable), the committee collectively should cover ERISA health/welfare and retirement plan expertise, and members should be able to evaluate plan expenses prudently.
  - The PAC Chair may consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify qualified candidates.

summary:
- Appendix Article PAC sets guiding principles for appointing members to PepsiCo’s Benefit Plan Committee (PAC) under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope: Supplements the plan document specifically on PAC member appointments.
- Eligibility criteria: Must be a PepsiCo employee at Leadership Group 1 or above, able to devote sufficient time, and possess the character and prudence to act solely in the interests of plan participants and beneficiaries.
- Additional PAC membership guidelines: 
  - Individual experience with benefit plan administration or transferable ERISA-related experience.
  - Collective committee expertise across ERISA health and welfare and retirement plan administration.
  - Ability to prudently evaluate plan-related expenses.
- Chair’s process: May consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify well-qualified candidates.
- Legal note: These guidelines are advisory for the Chair and do not alter ERISA’s legal standards.
- Exhibit 21: Begins a roster of PepsiCo, Inc. subsidiaries (as of Dec. 25, 2021) with entity names and jurisdictions spanning multiple countries and U.S. states, including numerous “Blue Cloud Distribution” state entities and other global subsidiaries; the list is partial in the excerpt.
text:
APPENDIX ARTICLE P AC
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments     
PAC.1 Scope.  This Article P AC supplements the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan document with respect to
the appointment of the members of the P AC.
PAC.2 General Guidelines . To be a member of the P AC, an individual must:
(a)    Be an employee of the PepsiCo Organization at a Leadership Group 1 or above level,
(b)    Be able to give adequate time to committee duties, and
(c)    Have the character and temperament to act prudently and diligently in the exclusive interest of the
Plan’ s participants and beneficiaries.
PAC.3 PAC Guidelines . In addition to satisfying the requirements set forth in Section P AC.2, the following
guidelines will also apply to the P AC membership:
(a)    Each member of the P AC should have experience with benefit plan administration or other
experience that can readily translate to a role concerning ERISA plan administration,
(b)    The membership of the P AC as a whole should have experience and expertise with respect to the
administration of ERISA health and welfare and retirement plans, and
(c)    Each member of the P AC should be capable of prudently evaluating the reasonableness of
expenses that are charged to the Plan.
PAC.4 Additional Information . The Chair of the P AC may seek information from Company personnel, including
the Controller , CFO and CHRO, in connection with his identification of well qualified candidates for committee
membership.

the P AC in the selection of committee members; however , they neither diminish nor enlarge the legal standard
applicable under ERISA.

- Purpose: A statutory Exhibit 21 listing PepsiCo, Inc.’s consolidated subsidiaries as of December 25, 2021.
- Format: An alphabetical roster of hundreds of legal entities paired with their jurisdictions of incorporation/organization.
- Scope of entities: Operating companies, bottling and concentrate manufacturers, sales and distribution arms, R&D and shared services centers, logistics, real estate, treasury/financing vehicles, holding companies, and captive insurance entities.
- Geographic breadth: Subsidiaries span North America (notably many U.S. Delaware entities and state-specific Blue Cloud Distribution companies), Latin America (e.g., Mexico, Guatemala, Argentina, Brazil, Peru, Chile, Colombia), Europe (e.g., UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Hungary, Czech Republic, Belgium, Cyprus, Switzerland, Russia, Ukraine, Serbia, Romania), Middle East & Africa (e.g., Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Nigeria, South Africa, Ethiopia), and Asia-Pacific (e.g., China, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand), plus Central Asia (e.g., Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan).
- Major brands/business units represented: Frito-Lay, Pepsi-Cola (bottling, manufacturing, and concentrate operations), Quaker Oats, Gatorade/Stokely-Van Camp, Walkers/Smith’s, Sabritas/Gamesa, Pioneer Foods, SodaStream, Tropicana/Alvalle, Evercrisp, Chipsy, Marbo, Lebedyansky and Wimm-Bill-Dann, Ceres, Baicaowei, Stacy’s, Health Warrior, Bare Foods, BFY Brands/PopCorners.
- Structural features: Extensive use of international holding and finance entities (e.g., in the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Ireland, Curaçao), multiple LLCs/B.V.s/GmbHs/S.à r.l.s across regions, captive insurers, pension trustee, and numerous specialized distribution, logistics, and promotional companies.
- Overall takeaway: The exhibit evidences PepsiCo’s global footprint and complex corporate structure supporting its diversified portfolio of beverages and foods through manufacturing, distribution, branding, and financial/administrative functions worldwide.

summary:
- Exhibit 24 – Power of Attorney: PepsiCo, Inc. and its undersigned officers and directors appoint David Flavell, Cynthia A. Nastanski, and Heather A. Hammond, each acting severally, as attorneys-in-fact to execute and file with the SEC, stock exchanges, and other authorities a broad range of documents on their behalf. Authorized filings include:
  - Numerous Automatic Shelf Registration Statements for PepsiCo common stock, debt securities, warrants, units, and guarantees.
  - Multiple registration statements related to acquisitions and exchange offers, including shares issued in connection with past transactions.
  - Registration statements for employee benefit, savings, 401(k), stock option, long-term incentive, director stock, and share award plans (including legacy Quaker, Tropicana, The Pepsi Bottling Group (PBG), and PepsiAmericas (PAS) plans).
  - Schedules 13E-3 related to merger transactions with PBG and PAS.
  - The Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 25, 2021, and all other required SEC reports and amendments (Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K), as well as filings needed for listing, registration, approval, and reporting of PepsiCo securities or guarantees.
  - The attorneys-in-fact may act with full authority, including substitution and revocation; the POA may be executed in counterparts, does not revoke prior powers of attorney unless expressly stated by date, and remains valid for each attorney-in-fact until they cease to be a PepsiCo employee. The POA is executed by PepsiCo and various executives and directors, including Chairman and CEO Ramon L. Laguarta, CFO Hugh F. Johnston, Principal Accounting Officer Marie T. Gallagher, and members of the Board, dated primarily February 9, 2022 (with some director signatures dated in 2021).

- Exhibit 31 – CEO Certification (SOX Section 302): Ramon L. Laguarta certifies, as of February 9, 2022, that he has reviewed PepsiCo’s Form 10-K; it contains no material misstatements or omissions; the financial statements fairly present the company’s financial condition, results, and cash flows; and that he and the other certifying officer:
  - Designed and evaluated disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting to ensure reliability and GAAP compliance.
  - Reported conclusions on control effectiveness and disclosed any changes in internal control over financial reporting during the most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect it.
  - Disclosed to auditors and the audit committee any significant deficiencies, material weaknesses, and any fraud involving management or employees with significant control responsibilities.

CERTIFICATION
I, Ramon L. Laguarta, certify that:
 
1.I have reviewed this annual report on Form 10-K of PepsiCo, Inc.;
2.Based on my knowledge, this report does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a material fact necessary to
make the statements made, in light of the circumstances under which such statements were made, not misleading with respect to the
period covered by this report;
3.Based on my knowledge, the financial statements, and other financial information included in this report, fairly present in all material
respects the financial condition, results of operations and cash flows of the registrant as of, and for, the periods presented in this report;
4.The registrant’s other certifying officer and I are responsible for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures (as
defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) and internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Exchange Act Rules
13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the registrant and have:
a)Designed such disclosure controls and procedures, or caused such disclosure controls and procedures to be designed under our
supervision, to ensure that material information relating to the registrant, including its consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to us
by others within those entities, particularly during the period in which this report is being prepared;
b)Designed such internal control over financial reporting, or caused such internal control over financial reporting to be designed under
our supervision, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial
statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles;
c)Evaluated the effectiveness of the registrant’s disclosure controls and procedures and presented in this report our conclusions about
the effectiveness of the disclosure controls and procedures, as of the end of the period covered by this report based on such
evaluation; and
d)Disclosed in this report any change in the registrant’s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the registrant’s
